rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright with your hands resting open on your thighs, and let your eyes close. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. On this path the breath is part of the teaching, so give it particular care. Feel the cool air coming in through the nostrils and the warmth of it leaving. Let the ribs widen and settle. If a hold becomes uncomfortable, shorten the count; nothing here should strain. With each outbreath, let go a little more: the face, the throat, the shoulders, the hands, the chest and belly, the legs and feet. When the body is loose and quiet and the breath flows easily, let your attention rest lightly at the centre of your chest, ready to build the first image.

rows.title: The Temple of Chokmah
rows.text: A temple forms around you. Its walls and floor are a soft, glowing grey, the Queen-scale colour of Chokmah, like pearl or high cloud lit from within. There is no roof. Above you a dark sky is crowded with the fixed stars, and the twelve signs of the zodiac wheel slowly across it. At the centre rises a single tall pillar of grey stone, with a small altar before it, and the air is warm with musk. Wheels of light turn at the edges of your vision: the Auphanim, the choir of this sphere. Stand before the pillar, breathe in, and vibrate the name Yah, letting the short syllable carry up to the stars. Then call Ratziel, archangel of Chokmah, herald of hidden wisdom. Sense a presence of great force and clarity, and ask for guidance and protection on the path.

rows.title: The Veil of the Fool
rows.text: In the east of the temple hangs a veil painted with Atu 0, The Fool: a horned, green-clad figure poised as if in the moment of a leap. Grapes lie at his feet, a tiger is at his leg and a crocodile waits in the water below, and around him are spirals of colour, a dove, a vulture and a butterfly. Stand before it. With your right forefinger, trace the letter Aleph, א, in bright pale yellow light, the King-scale colour of this path: first the long diagonal from upper left to lower right, then the arm at the upper right and the leg at the lower left. Let it hang shining in the air. Vibrate its name, Aleph. The veil stirs as though a wind has risen behind it. Step through the letter and the image, and let them close behind you.

rows.title: The Open Sky
rows.text: There is no road. You are in open sky, clear and bright, washed in pale yellow light that shades into sky blue in every direction. Yet you do not fall. The air holds you as water holds a floating leaf. A steady wind moves around you, and you notice that it moves through you as well, entering with each breath and leaving with the next, until the boundary between you and the sky feels thin. Here and there the blue deepens into streaks of blue-emerald green, and green flecked with gold glitters at the edges of sight like sunlight on moving leaves. This is the Scintillating Intelligence: everything flickers and nothing settles. Let the wind carry you forward and upward without trying too hard to steer.

rows.title: The Ox, the Eagle and the Sylphs
rows.text: An eagle rises beside you on the same current, wings still, eye fixed ahead. Below you a great ox walks calmly across the sky as though it were a field, patient and enormous. Aleph means ox: the strength that pulls the plough is here too, quiet and unhurried. Now you glimpse slender, quick shapes in the wind itself. They flicker at the edges of your vision and vanish when you look straight at them: the sylphs, the beings of Air. A small island of earth drifts past carrying a stand of aspens, every leaf trembling and flashing silver. Somewhere a honey-coloured topaz glints in the light. The sharp, green scent of galbanum passes on the breeze and is gone.

rows.title: Within the Trump
rows.text: The wind carries you into the heart of the trump. Colours spiral outward from a centre you cannot quite find, pale yellow and blue and green, turning like breath made visible. A dove passes, then a vulture circling high above, then a butterfly that looks too fragile for such a wind and yet is untroubled by it. Heavy clusters of grapes hang in the air, sweet-smelling. Far below, water glints, and a crocodile lies in it, still and patient. A tiger paces nearby, its stripes like flame. None of these creatures threatens you; each one is simply present and complete. Notice how it feels to be here with no plan, no task and nowhere to go but this moment, and let any habit of bracing yourself loosen.

rows.title: The Guide
rows.text: A figure comes toward you from the centre of the spiral. It may appear as the Fool himself, green-clad and horned, light on his feet. It may appear as Hoor-pa-kraat, Harpocrates, a child seated on a lotus with a finger to his lips. Greet it with courtesy. If you want to test it, trace Aleph in pale yellow light between you and notice how the figure meets the sign. Then ask what this path has to teach you, and wait. The answer may come as a word, a gesture, a sound, a silence, or an object placed in your open hands. Receive whatever comes without judging it, improving it or deciding in advance what it ought to be. Take the time you need, and when the exchange is complete, give thanks.

rows.title: The Threshold of Kether
rows.text: The wind grows quiet, and the light ahead becomes so bright that the yellow and blue dissolve into pure white brilliance. This is the threshold of Kether, the Crown. You do not cross it. Stand, or float, at the edge and look. You may see a single point of light, or a vast swirling motion like the first stirring of the heavens, or the profile of an ancient bearded king with his other side turned away. You may see only brightness. Notice that the breath you have followed all along seems to begin here, before it becomes wind. Do not reach for it or try to keep it. Let a little of its stillness enter you, then bow and turn back.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Let the wind carry you back the way you came. The guide may go with you or stay; either is right. You pass the spirals, the tiger and the crocodile, the dove and the vulture, the aspens, the eagle and the patient ox, while the white light behind you softens to pale yellow and then to sky blue. Ahead you see the back of the veil with its green figure. Step through into the grey temple of Chokmah and feel your feet firmly on its floor. Turn to the veil and trace Aleph in reverse, last stroke first, watching the light dissolve until the cloth is plain. Face the pillar and thank Ratziel for guidance and protection. Let the temple fade gently into darkness.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Take a slow, full breath and let it go with a sigh. After so much air, let yourself grow heavy, like the ox. Feel the weight of your body on the seat and your feet flat on the floor. Notice the temperature of the room and the sounds around you. Wriggle your fingers and toes, stretch your arms and shoulders, and open your eyes. Look at a few ordinary objects and name them silently. Press your palms against the floor or stamp your feet. Before you do anything else, write down what you experienced, above all whatever the guide gave you, while the details are still clear.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in your chosen posture, spine straight, hands resting on your thighs, and let your eyes close. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the rhythm even, not forced; if the holds strain, shorten the count. With each outbreath, let one part of the body soften: brow and jaw, throat and shoulders, arms and hands, chest and belly, hips, legs and feet. Feel the weight of your body resting on the seat and the floor. Let the sounds of the room come and go without following them. When the breath runs by itself and the body is heavy and still, gather your attention just behind the eyes, as if you stood at the edge of a quiet space that is ready to be built.

rows.title: The Temple of Binah
rows.text: A temple forms around you. Its walls and floor are black, the Queen-scale colour of Binah. It is not a hard or empty black but the deep, living dark of still water at night, and it holds you the way the sea holds a swimmer. On a plain altar at the centre burns a single crimson flame, and the air is heavy and sweet with myrrh. Beside the altar stands the image of this sphere: a mature woman, robed and silent, her stillness older than the stones. At the edges of the dark sit great still forms, the Aralim, the choir of this sphere. A quiet sorrow may hang in the air; let it be. Face the altar, breathe in, and vibrate YHVH Elohim (Yod He Vau He Elohim) until the walls seem to hum. Then call Tzaphkiel, archangel of Binah, and ask for guardianship on the path.

rows.title: The Veil of the Magus
rows.text: In the east of the temple, where a wall should be, hangs a veil. As you come closer you see that it is painted with Atu I, The Magus: a young figure caught in swift motion, winged at the feet, with the tools of magic wheeling in the air around him, a caduceus rising behind him and the dog-headed ape of Thoth crouched below. Stand before it. With your right forefinger, trace the letter Beth, ב, in clear yellow light, the King-scale colour of this path: a roof, a wall and a floor, a house open on its left side. Let the letter hang shining in the air. Vibrate its name, Beth, and feel the sound pass into the cloth. The veil thins and brightens like light through glass. Step forward through the letter and the image, and let them close behind you.

rows.title: The Transparent Way
rows.text: You stand at the foot of a path that climbs steeply into clear, brilliant air. Everything is steeped in yellow light, the King-scale colour, shading at the edges into deep purple, the Queen scale, as though dawn and dusk were happening together. The path underfoot seems to be made of glass, or of air made firm, and through it you see yellow depths falling away below. This is the Intelligence of Transparency, which the old commentary links with the place that visions come from. Nothing here is hidden and nothing blocks the way. Notice how your own thoughts behave in this air: do they come sharp and quick, or do they cloud over? Threads of grey and violet light drift at the edges of sight, and the air carries the clean, resinous scent of mastic and storax. Walk slowly.

rows.title: The Creatures of Mercury
rows.text: As you climb, the path grows lively. Swallows cut past you, fast and exact, turning on currents you cannot see. On a ledge an ibis stands on one leg, its long curved bill tilted as though it were reading something written in the air. Further on sits a baboon, the cynocephalus sacred to Thoth, hands on its knees, watching you with bright, intelligent eyes. When you pause, it copies your posture. Low plants of vervain and marjoram edge the path, and a single palm leans out from the rock. In the cliff face a vein of opal catches the light and shifts through fiery colours as you pass. Above you the sign of Mercury turns slowly, crescent over circle over cross: the mark of the one who carries messages between the worlds.

rows.title: The House of the Word
rows.text: The path levels out onto an open height where the air almost rings, like the note of a struck glass. Here the picture on the veil comes to life around you. The tools of the art circle in a slow, wide orbit: a wand, a cup, a sword, a disc, a stylus, a scroll. Each one passes close to you and moves away again. Behind them stands a caduceus, a staff of light wound with two serpents whose heads meet beneath outspread wings. Remember that Beth means house, and that the Hebrew scriptures begin with this letter. Sense the whole path as that kind of house: a shelter where the first impulse of the Crown becomes a word that can be spoken and heard. Stay here a while and listen beneath the ringing.

rows.title: The Guide
rows.text: A figure steps out of the circling light: a youth, lithe and quick, winged at heel and helmet, carrying the caduceus. Some see him as Hermes, some as ibis-headed Thoth with the scribe's palette, some as both at once. Greet him courteously. If you want to test him, trace Beth in yellow light between you and watch how he meets the sign; a true guide of this path is at ease with it. Then ask him plainly what this path has to teach you, and listen. He may speak, show you a scene, or place a word, a symbol or an object in your hands. Receive whatever comes without judging it and without trying to shape it. Take all the time you need. When the exchange feels complete, thank him.

rows.title: The Threshold of Kether
rows.text: The guide turns and points upward. The path ends at a threshold where the yellow air becomes too bright to hold any colour at all. Beyond it is pure white brilliance, the light of Kether, the Crown. You do not cross. You stand at the edge and look. You may glimpse a single point of light, or a vast, slow swirling like the first motion of the heavens, or the profile of an ancient bearded king whose other side is never shown. You may see only the light itself. Do not strain toward it and do not try to keep it. Let a little of its stillness settle into you, the way sunlight warms a stone. When you have looked long enough, bow and turn away.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Walk back down the path the way you came. The guide may go with you or stay above; either is fine. You pass the circling tools, the ape, the ibis on its ledge, the vein of opal and the swallows, while the brilliance behind you softens to yellow and then to deepening purple. Ahead you see the back of the veil, bright with the Magus. Step through into the black temple of Binah and feel its floor beneath you. Turn to face the veil. Trace Beth in reverse, from the last stroke to the first, and watch the light withdraw until the cloth is plain and dark. Face the altar and its crimson flame, and thank Tzaphkiel for guarding your way. Let the temple fade gently into darkness.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Notice your breath, a little fuller now. Feel the weight of your body on the seat, your feet on the floor and the temperature of the air on your skin. Hear the ordinary sounds of the room. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, stretch if you need to, and open your eyes when you are ready. Look around and silently name a few plain objects you can see. Press your palms to the floor or stamp your feet lightly. Before you do anything else, write down what you saw, heard and received, above all whatever the guide gave you, while it is still fresh.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright with your spine straight, feet flat on the floor, palms resting on your thighs. Close your eyes. Take up the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, rest empty for four. Let the rhythm settle until it needs no effort. With each out-breath, release tension from the top down: forehead, eyes, jaw, throat, shoulders, arms, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. Notice the coolness or warmth of the air and the small sounds of the room, and let them recede. This path asks for stillness above all, so take your time here. When body and breath are quiet, let the count dissolve and rest in simple awareness.

rows.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
rows.text: Around you a temple takes shape. Its walls and floor are clear gold, as if sunlight had been made solid. It is six-sided, and the warm air carries the scent of frankincense. At the centre stands an altar with a single steady flame. On the wall beyond it you see the magical image of this sphere: a majestic king, a child, a crucified god. One of these faces may come forward more strongly than the others. Stand before the altar and vibrate the divine name of Tiphareth: YHVH Eloah va-Daath (Yod Heh Vav Heh Eh-loh-ah vah-Dah-ath). Let it fill the golden room. Then call on the archangel Raphael. Feel a bright, clear presence, like fresh air full of sunlight, take its place beside you as guardian of your journey.

rows.title: The Veil of Gimel
rows.text: Beyond the altar, in the eastern wall, hangs a tall curtain of deep blue shot with silver. Painted on it is Atu II, The Priestess. A woman sits with her arms lifted, and from them a veil of shimmering light falls around her like a net of dew; it is all she wears. A bow lies across her knees, a camel stands at her feet, and seeds and crystals are scattered below. Look at the painting until it feels present and alive. Then raise your hand and trace the letter Gimel ג large on the curtain, in pure bright blue: a tall upright stroke with a short foot stepping out at its base. Vibrate the letter's name, Gimel (Gim-mel, with a hard G). The blue letter flares, the curtain parts down its centre, and you step through.

rows.title: The Moonlit Desert
rows.text: You come out under a night sky of deep, clear blue. A full Moon hangs high ahead, and its silver light lies across a wide, pale desert. The sand is cool underfoot and faintly luminous: silver, shading to a cold pale blue where the dunes fold. There is almost no wind. The path is not a road. Instead, a single line of moonlight runs straight ahead across the sand, rising gently, and you know it leads up to the crown of the Tree. This is the longest of all the paths, climbing the Middle Pillar from the Sun to the Crown. The silence is complete. Stand here for a while and let the cold, clean air and the silver light wash through you.

rows.title: The Camel
rows.text: A camel kneels on the sand beside the line of light, pale in the moonlight, calm and patient, with a saddle-cloth of blue and silver on its back. Gimel means camel: the creature that crosses the desert carrying its own water. Approach it slowly, rest a hand on its warm neck, and mount. It rises with a rocking motion and walks, unhurried, along the silver line. Feel its steady gait beneath you. For a while a lean, pale dog, a hound of the huntress, keeps pace at your side, then drops back. At the edges of the dunes, faint shapes may drift like mist or half-remembered faces. Let them pass without giving them your attention. Keep your gaze on the Moon.

rows.title: The Uniting Intelligence
rows.text: The desert grows wider and emptier. The ground falls away on either side, and you realise the camel is walking a narrow ridge across a great gulf: the Abyss, where the middle of the Tree seems to open into darkness. Do not look down for long. The moonlight holds the path firm. Small things glint in the sand as you pass: a pearl, a moonstone, a clear crystal, the grey-green leaves of mugwort, an almond branch in flower, a small ranunculus. The air carries a faint, clean scent of camphor. This path is called the Uniting Intelligence, the essence of glory and the fulfilment of the truth of spiritual things. Feel how it binds the heart of the Tree to its source with a single cord of silver light.

rows.title: The Priestess
rows.text: Ahead, where the ridge meets the far side, a figure waits in the moonlight. The camel kneels and you dismount. She is the Priestess. She sits veiled in a web of shimmering light that falls from her raised arms like a curtain of dew and starlight. She wears a lunar crown, and a bow rests across her knees. At her feet lie seeds, fruits and crystals, the first beginnings of form. You may instead see Artemis with her bow and hounds, or Khonsu, the young Egyptian moon god crowned with disc and crescent. Let the form come as it will. Greet her quietly. Ask what this path teaches, and what you must become to walk it. Then be still, and let her answer come as words, an image, a gesture or silence.

rows.title: The Threshold of Kether
rows.text: Thank her. Behind her, the silver line runs a short way further to the very top of the Tree. Go to its edge and stop. Above and before you is a brilliance so pure it has no colour: white beyond white, a single point that is also everywhere. You sense the first stirrings of motion, the Primum Mobile, where all turning begins. Silently, the divine name Eheieh, 'I am', sounds within you. Do not try to enter the light or hold on to it. Look only for as long as is comfortable. Then lower your eyes, bow, and turn back.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: The Priestess, or whatever form met you, has withdrawn into the veil of light. The camel is waiting. Mount again and ride back down the silver line, over the ridge across the gulf and through the pale desert under the Moon. The way back is quicker. Dismount where you began, thank the camel, and walk to the painted curtain of the Priestess standing in the sand. Step through it into the golden temple of Tiphareth. Turn and trace the letter Gimel once more in blue, then watch it fade into the cloth as the curtain closes. Turn to the altar and thank the archangel Raphael for guarding your way. Let the golden temple dim and dissolve.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Feel your body again, heavier after the thin air of the path. Notice the chair beneath you, the floor under your feet, the temperature of the room. Breathe a little deeper and a little faster than before. Move your fingers and toes and stretch your arms. Rub your palms together until they are warm, and press them gently over your eyes. Open your eyes and look at something solid and ordinary, naming it to yourself. Stamp your feet or press them firmly into the floor. Before anything else, write down the guide's word or symbol and whatever you saw, heard or felt, however slight. Lunar impressions fade quickly, like dreams on waking.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs. If you know the god-form posture, you can use that. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold full for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the count grow slow and even. With each out-breath, let one part of the body soften: the jaw, then the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs. Notice your weight settling into the chair and the floor. Let the day's thoughts pass without following them. When breath and body are quiet, let the count go and simply breathe, aware of the room around you and the stillness gathering inside.

rows.title: The Temple of Binah
rows.text: Before you a temple forms. Its walls, floor and vaulted roof are black. The black is not empty but full, a soft deep darkness like the sea at night. Low crimson lamps burn in niches, and the air is heavy with myrrh. Far off you hear the slow breathing of waves. At the centre stands a black altar with a cup on it. Behind the altar stands the magical image of this sphere: a mature woman, grave and calm, the Great Mother. Stand before the altar and vibrate the divine name of Binah: YHVH Elohim (Yod Heh Vav Heh Eh-loh-heem). Feel it roll out into the darkness. Then call on the archangel Tzaphkiel, the Beholder of God. Sense a vast, quiet presence, like a hooded shadow, take its place beside you as witness and guardian.

rows.title: The Veil of Daleth
rows.text: Behind the altar, in the far wall, is a doorway hung with a heavy curtain. Painted on it is Atu III, The Empress. A crowned woman sits enthroned among greens, blues and rose. Her arms and body form a circle crossed by a bar. A sparrow and a dove are beside her, a pelican at her feet, and an arched gateway behind her. Look at the painting until it seems to breathe. Then raise your hand and trace the letter Daleth ד large on the curtain, in brilliant emerald green: a level roof with a single leg dropping from its right-hand end. Vibrate the letter's name, Daleth (Dah-leth), and feel it resound. Daleth means door, and the curtain swings open like one. You step through.

rows.title: The Level Road
rows.text: You step out into morning light. A path leads through green country, the emerald of new leaves and the soft green of early spring, under an open sky of clear, soft blue. The air is mild and smells of damp earth and something sweet. The ground rolls in gentle folds, and small springs run through the grass. Now and then the light takes on a flush of rose, shot through with pale yellow rays, as if dawn and blossom were one colour. You notice that you are neither climbing nor descending. This road runs level across the very top of the Tree, from the Mother's darkness towards the Father's grey radiance. Walk slowly. Feel the ground under your feet and the warmth on your face, and notice how easily everything here grows.

rows.title: Myrtle, Rose and Dove
rows.text: The path runs between hedges of glossy, fragrant myrtle and wild roses that open as you watch. Clover covers the ground at your feet. Sparrows dart and chatter in the branches. A pair of white doves lands on the path ahead and walks in front of you for a while. Further on, a still pool lies among reeds, and a swan moves across it without leaving a ripple. The water is the blue-green of turquoise, and on its bed you glimpse a stone of deep emerald. A light wind carries the scent of sandalwood and rose. Let each thing be exactly itself, and notice its colour, texture and sound. Nothing here asks you to hurry. Everything is making something: leaf, flower, egg, seed.

rows.title: The Illuminating Intelligence
rows.text: The path opens onto a meadow. At its centre stands a throne whose pillars rise in twisting shapes, like flames of green and gold. Behind it an arched gateway frames the sky. The throne is empty for now, but the scene of the card is laid out around its foot. A pelican stands over her nest, piercing her own breast to feed her young. Beside her leans a shield bearing a white, double-headed eagle. A lotus lies on the seat. This is the fourteenth path, called the Illuminating Intelligence: the light in which the hidden foundations of holy things first take shape. Stand quietly before the throne. Feel the green light around you thicken and soften, the way light might just before it becomes a form.

rows.title: The Empress
rows.text: A presence gathers on the throne, and a woman is seated there: the Empress. Her robes shift between green and blue. Her arms and body together make the shape of a circle crossed by a bar, the alchemical sign of Salt. A sparrow and a dove rest near her, and she takes up the lotus. You may instead see Hathor, cow-horned with the sun's disc between her horns, or Aphrodite. Let whatever form comes, come. Greet her with respect. Ask her what this path teaches, and what you need to know about love and making. Then be silent and receptive. She may speak, show you something, or give you a symbol or a word. Receive it without judging it, and remember it.

rows.title: The Threshold of Chokmah
rows.text: When the exchange feels complete, thank her. Beyond the throne the gateway stands open, and the path runs a little further to a threshold. Walk to it and stop at the edge. Before you lies a vast, soft grey radiance, pearl and silver. Within it is a pale, pure blue, like the sky seen from a great height. Points of light turn slowly inside it: the wheeling of the fixed stars and the zodiac. You sense a force that is pure outgoing will, restless and bright, the Father's energy before it takes any form. Somewhere within you, the short divine name Yah sounds. Do not enter. Take in only what comes, bow to the threshold, and turn around.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Walk back along the level road the way you came. Pass the empty throne and the pelican's nest, the pool and the swan, the roses and the myrtle. The doves lift away as you pass. The green light feels gentle and familiar now. Ahead you see the painted curtain of the Empress standing in the meadow like a door without a wall. Step through it into the black temple of Binah. Turn to face the curtain and trace the letter Daleth over it once more. Watch the emerald letter sink into the fabric as the curtain falls closed. Turn to the altar and thank the archangel Tzaphkiel for guarding you, and feel the dark, still presence withdraw. Let the temple dim and fade.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Become aware of your body again: its weight in the chair, your feet on the floor, your hands where they rest. Feel the breath moving in and out on its own. Listen to the sounds of the room and the world outside. Take a few deeper breaths, and with each one become more fully present. Move your fingers and toes and roll your shoulders. When you are ready, open your eyes and look around, naming a few ordinary things you see. Stamp your feet lightly on the floor. Before you do anything else, write down what you saw, heard and felt, especially the guide's word or symbol, while it is still fresh.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat, hands open on your thighs, head balanced lightly on the spine. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the count be slow and exact. This path belongs to air, so attend to the breath itself: its coolness as it enters, its warmth as it leaves. With each exhalation loosen one region of the body: the face and eyes, the throat, the shoulders, the chest, the belly, the hips and legs. Imagine the body as a clear vessel, emptying of tension the way a cup empties when it is tipped. Let outside sounds pass through you. When the breath is even and the body feels light and settled, release the count and rest.

rows.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
rows.text: Around you a temple forms, six-sided, its walls glowing a clear golden yellow, the Queen-scale colour of Tiphareth. Sunlight seems to come from everywhere at once, though no sun is visible. The floor is inlaid with a great hexagram. At its centre stands a cubic altar bearing a Rose Cross, a red rose blooming where its arms meet. The air is rich with olibanum. On the walls are three images: a majestic king, a child, and a god upon a cross, three faces of this sphere. Let the room grow steady and bright. Then draw a full breath and vibrate the God-name: YHVH Eloah va-Daath. Feel it fill all six walls. Call the archangel Raphael, and see a tall presence form beside you, robed in yellow shot with violet, bringing a cool, clean breeze like morning air.

rows.title: The Window of He
rows.text: Raphael leads you to one wall, where a tall curtain hangs. It is painted with Atu XVII of the Thoth deck, The Star: a woman beneath a night sky of blue and violet, pouring from two cups, a great seven-pointed star above her. Study it until it is vivid. Raise your hand and trace the letter He on the cloth in violet light, the King-scale colour of Aquarius, which travels to this path with the Star: a flat roof across the top, a long leg descending on the right, and a short separate leg on the left that does not quite reach the roof, a window with a gap for the light. Vibrate its name: He. The letter shines steadily. The curtain draws aside onto an open window full of night. Raphael remains, keeping the way. Climb through.

rows.title: Between Land and Water
rows.text: You stand at the edge of a vast, still night. The light here is violet, soft and cool, and the air has the pale clear blue of a sky just before dawn, though stars shine everywhere above you. Breathe it in: clean, fresh, perfectly still, air that holds its shape. Beneath your feet the ground is scattered with crystals, clear and faceted, catching the starlight. The path runs gently upward along a shoreline where calm water meets the land. Olive trees grow beside it, their silver-green leaves pale in the violet light. Among them a peacock steps slowly, then opens its tail: a hundred eyes of blue and green and bronze, each one a small watching star. Walk slowly. Notice the silence, and how far you can see.

rows.title: The Constituting Intelligence
rows.text: A green, resinous, faintly bitter scent reaches you: galbanum, rising from a censer that hangs from a low olive branch, its smoke curling upward in slow spirals. Beneath it, on a flat rock, lie a smooth stone of milky blue chalcedony and a sphere of clear glass. Pick up the glass and look through it. The stars seem nearer, and the darkness between them grows deeper and richer, not empty but full. The Sepher Yetzirah names this path the Constituting Intelligence, said to constitute the substance of creation in pure darkness. Let your attention rest not on the stars but on the dark between them, the ground from which every point of light stands out. Feel that darkness as something that holds rather than something that hides. Then set the glass down where you found it.

rows.title: The Star Pours
rows.text: Ahead, where the shore curves, a woman stands at the meeting of land and water. Her skin holds the faint blue of the night sky, and her hair falls long about her. In one hand she raises a cup of gold and pours; in the other she holds a cup of silver, pouring low, so that two shining streams fall, mingle, and run out over the land and into the still water. Behind her turns a great celestial globe, and above it blazes a seven-pointed star. All around her the light moves in slow spirals, as if space itself were curling. Watch the water fall. Notice where it lands and what it touches. Crowley names this figure Nuit, the star-goddess of infinite space, and the Book of the Law tells you that every man and every woman is a star.

rows.title: The Daughter of the Firmament
rows.text: She turns and sees you. Approach slowly and stop at a respectful distance; the water runs past your feet, cool and bright. This is the Daughter of the Firmament, the Dweller between the Waters. Greet her simply, then ask: what does this path teach? Be still and wait. The answer may come as words, a picture, a feeling, a colour, or a movement of the water. She may offer you something from one of her cups, or show you a single star and let you look at it. Take what is given without deciding yet what it means, and hold it clearly in memory. If anything in the figure seems wrong or strained, trace He in violet between you and watch how it responds: a true image grows steadier, a false one falters. If nothing comes, stay and listen. Take all the time you need.

rows.title: The Edge of the Abyss
rows.text: When the meeting feels complete, thank her. The path continues past her, rising into open night, until the land simply stops. Before you lies the Abyss, a gulf that is less dark than absent. Do not step off the edge. Stand, and look across. Far beyond, a great sphere of soft grey light glows, pearly and iridescent, touched with pure soft blue. Around it the whole wheel of the zodiac turns, and every star you have seen tonight seems to draw its light from there, as if from a fountain. This is Chokmah, Wisdom, the sphere of the fixed stars, where the name Yah resounds and the archangel Ratziel keeps the secrets of God. Let its radiance reach you across the gulf. Remain on this side. When you have seen enough, turn back.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Walk back down the path at the pace you came. Pass the woman, still pouring; the globe and the seven-pointed star; the censer of galbanum and the glass sphere on its rock; the olive trees and the peacock, its tail now folded. The crystals glint underfoot. Ahead you see the window you climbed through, framed in golden light. Climb back into the six-sided temple of Tiphareth. Turn to face the window and the painted Star. Trace He in violet once more, and this time watch it fade gently into the cloth as the curtain falls closed. Turn to Raphael and thank the archangel for keeping the way. Bow to the altar and the Rose Cross. Let the golden walls grow transparent, and let the temple dissolve into light, and then into quiet.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Come back into your body. Notice the chair beneath you, the floor under your feet, the temperature of the room on your skin. Take a few ordinary, deeper breaths, slightly quicker than before. Move your fingers and toes, stretch your neck and shoulders, and let the sounds of the room return fully. Open your eyes and look at something solid and familiar, naming it to yourself. Press your feet firmly into the floor and stamp them twice. Then, before anything else, write down what you experienced: the Star's answer, anything you were given, the colours, scents and sounds, and any surprises. Later, compare your record with the symbol list for this path.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs, spine tall but not stiff. Let your eyes close. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count slow and even. With each out-breath, let one part of the body soften: the jaw, the brow, the shoulders and arms, the belly, the legs. Notice the weight of the body pressing into the chair and the feet pressing into the floor, the way a bull stands in its field: heavy, patient, unhurried. Let the sounds of the room come and go without following them. When the breath runs by itself and the body feels settled and warm, let the count fall away and rest in the stillness.

rows.title: The Temple of Chesed
rows.text: Around you a temple takes shape: square, four walls of deep clear blue, the Queen-scale colour of Chesed, rising to a vault flecked with violet. The floor is cool blue stone and the air smells of cedar. Against the far wall stands a throne, and on it sits a mighty king, crowned and enthroned, broad-shouldered and generous of face, a sceptre in his hand. Before him a low altar holds a wand and a shepherd's crook. Take in the room slowly until it is steady. Then draw the breath deep and vibrate the God-name of this sphere, sending the sound out to all four walls: El. Feel the stone hum with it. Call on the archangel Tzadkiel, the Righteousness of God, and see a tall figure robed in blue and violet gather at your side, the soft glitter of the Chashmalim about him.

rows.title: The Veil of the Hierophant
rows.text: Tzadkiel leads you to the right of the throne, where a heavy curtain hangs in the wall. Painted on it is Atu V of the Thoth deck, The Hierophant: a figure enthroned above a bull, a tall window behind him, a woman standing before him. Look until the image is clear. Raise your hand and, with a finger of light, trace the letter Vau on the curtain: a single upright stroke with a short head turning to the left, like a nail or a hook. Draw it in red-orange, the King-scale colour of this path, and see it burn steadily against the cloth. Vibrate the letter's name: Vau. The curtain stirs as if breathed upon and parts down the middle. Tzadkiel remains at the threshold, keeping the door. Step through.

rows.title: The Red-Orange Road
rows.text: Beyond the veil you stand on a broad road of packed earth. The soil is a rich brown and the fields on either side a deep warm olive. The light is red-orange, low and steady like an evening that does not end, and above it the sky deepens to indigo. The road rises gently. Mallow grows along the verges, soft-leaved, its pale flowers nodding at your ankles. Ahead, giant trees stand at intervals beside the way, trunks so broad that several people could not circle them, roots gripping deep. Walk slowly and feel the ground take your weight with each step. In a field to one side a great bull grazes. It lifts its head and regards you, calm and immovable, then returns to the grass. Notice how much quiet there is here.

rows.title: The Triumphal Intelligence
rows.text: The air grows sweet with storax, warm and balsamic, seeping as resin from the bark of the great trees. Where the road passes between two of them, a wooden gate stands open, hung on heavy iron nails driven cleanly into the posts. Pause and look at the nails. Each one joins two things that would otherwise fall apart; in Hebrew the letter Vau is also the word for 'and'. Set into one gatepost is a large topaz, golden-brown, taking in the red light and giving it back softer. Rest your hand on it. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this the Triumphal or Eternal Intelligence: a delight in glory with nothing beyond it, a garden made ready for the just. Let that settle without forcing a meaning. Feel a joy that does not flare and fade, but stays, the way the earth stays.

rows.title: The Temple of the Hierophant
rows.text: Beyond the gate the road climbs to a hall of dark indigo stone. Inside, red-orange light falls through a tall oriel window whose upper frame is fastened with nine great nails; above it you can make out a serpent and a dove. Beneath the window a throne rests upon a bull, and elephants stand patiently on either side. In the four corners of the hall the four living creatures, a man, a lion, an eagle and a bull, face the throne. On it sits the Hierophant. On his breast a six-rayed star holds a five-pointed one, and within it a small child dances. His hand holds a wand crowned with three interlocking rings. Before him stands a woman girt with a sword, upright and unafraid. Take in each detail slowly. Nothing here is hurried.

rows.title: The Ancient Speaks
rows.text: The Hierophant turns his face toward you. He is an Ancient, crowned and sceptred, his hand raised in blessing, and his expression is hard to read; there may be a smile at its edge. Approach with respect and stand before him, beside the woman with the sword. Greet him in whatever way feels right, then ask plainly: what does this path teach? Be still and listen. The answer may come as words, an image, a gesture, or a sensation in the body; it may come from him, from the woman, or from the child. He may place something in your hands. Receive whatever is given without judging it, and remember it exactly. Should anything feel wrong, trace Vau in red-orange before it and watch how it responds. If nothing seems to come, simply stay. Silence here is also an answer.

rows.title: The First Nail over the Abyss
rows.text: When the exchange feels complete, bow, and pass through a door beside the oriel window. The road continues upward and soon becomes a bridge, fastened plank by plank with iron nails, reaching out over a gulf whose bottom you cannot see. This is the Abyss. Go no farther than the first nail. Stand there and look across. Far beyond the gulf glows a soft grey light, iridescent like pearl and shot through with pure soft blue. Within it great wheels turn slowly, set with the stars of the zodiac, and you may sense a single outpouring force, immense and without shape. This is Chokmah, Wisdom, where the name Yah is spoken and the archangel Ratziel keeps the secrets of God. Let the sight touch you. Do not cross. When you have seen what you can, turn back.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Retrace your steps at the same unhurried pace: off the bridge, through the door, past the throne where the Hierophant sits as before, and out beneath the oriel window. Walk down the road, through the gate on its iron nails, past the topaz and the weeping storax. The giant trees go by one by one; the bull still grazes. Ahead the veil appears, painted with Atu V. Pass through it into the blue square temple of Chesed. Turn to face the veil and trace Vau upon it once more, this time watching the red-orange letter dim and sink back into the cloth until the curtain hangs closed and still. Turn to Tzadkiel and thank the archangel for keeping the way. Bow to the enthroned king. Let the blue walls grow faint and transparent, and dissolve.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Become aware of your body in the chair: the weight of your hands on your thighs, your feet on the floor, the air moving at your nostrils. Take three deeper breaths, a little quicker than before. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and let the sounds of the room return. When you are ready, open your eyes and look around, naming a few ordinary objects to yourself. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor, twice. Before you do anything else, write down what you saw, heard and received, especially the Hierophant's answer and anything placed in your hands, while the memory is fresh. Later, compare your notes with the symbol list for this path.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright on a firm chair with your feet flat on the floor and your hands resting palm-down on your thighs. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. This is a path of Air, and the lungs belong to it, so let your attention rest on them. Feel them fill from the base upward and empty from the top down, the two sides of the chest moving together as a pair. Round by round, let the body soften: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, hands, belly, legs and feet. Let the faint bitterness of the incense mark the edge of the ordinary room. When the breathing has become steady and unforced, rest there for a while.

rows.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
rows.text: A six-sided hall of gold forms around you. Its walls glow with the clear yellow of the Queen scale. The light has no single source, as if the air itself were sunlit. The floor is warm underfoot. In the centre stands an altar shaped as a double cube and draped in white, with a small flame burning steadily on it. Above the altar the image of this sphere shifts gently as you watch: a majestic king, then a child, then a god with arms outstretched as on a cross. It settles into whichever form is clearest to you. Breathe in the sweet resin of olibanum. Vibrate the God-name so that it fills all six walls: Yod He Vau He Eloah va-Daath. Call the archangel: Raphael. A tall figure in yellow touched with violet stands beside you, and the air feels fresh and healing. Ask Raphael to guard the temple and your return.

rows.title: The Veil of the Lovers
rows.text: A curtain hangs in the eastern wall, painted with Atu VI, The Lovers. A hooded figure spreads his arms over a crowned king and queen. There are a lion and an eagle, two children, a winged egg with a serpent wound around it, and a winged archer overhead, all beneath an arch of swords. Stand in front of the curtain. With your right forefinger, trace the letter Zain in bright orange light: a single upright stroke topped by a short crossbar, like a sword standing on its point. Vibrate its name: Zain. As the sound fades, the painted figures seem to breathe. The curtain parts down its centre into two equal halves. Step between them and let them close behind you.

rows.title: The Twin Roads
rows.text: You are standing on a road washed in orange light, bright and restless as the air at noon. After a few paces the road divides into two lanes running side by side, separated only by a thin line of light. Then they join, then divide again, over and over. Walk in whichever lane you choose, and notice that you can see the other one clearly the whole time. A light wind moves constantly, carrying voices you cannot quite make out. A magpie watches you from a post, black and white at once. Further along, hybrid creatures wander calmly: a striped horse, a bird that cannot fly. Orchids grow along the verges. The old text calls this the Disposing Intelligence, which disposes the upright toward faith. Notice what in you is being sorted and set in order.

rows.title: The Royal Marriage
rows.text: The roads join for the last time in a hall under a high arch of swords, their blades pointing down, bright and quiet. The scene from the veil stands alive before you. A dark king crowned with gold holds a lance, and a red lion walks beside him. A pale queen crowned with silver holds a cup, and an eagle as white as frost stands beside her. A hooded figure between and above them extends his arms over both, and their hands are joined beneath his. Two children, one dark and one fair, stand at their feet holding flowers and a club. In the centre of the floor rests an egg with wings, a serpent wound around it. At the very top, a winged child draws a bow. Two women's shapes are half-seen at the edges, one pale and one dark. Take it all in slowly.

rows.title: The Tripod
rows.text: Beyond the pair, in a quieter recess, a bronze tripod stands over a shallow bowl. A thin thread of bitter smoke rises from it: wormwood. This is the seat of the oracle, the tripod of Apollo the Diviner. Breathe slowly. Feel your lungs take in the smoke-scented air and give it back, one movement in two halves. Look up through the arch and you see two bright stars close together. They are Castor and Pollux, the twins of Gemini, one mortal and one immortal in the old story, who chose to share their fate. A clear crystal lies on the rim of the bowl, and through it everything appears twice. Beside it, a darker stone changes colour as the light shifts, from green to red. Notice how everything here comes in pairs.

rows.title: The Officiant
rows.text: The hooded figure turns from the king and queen and comes toward you. His robe is covered in fine writing you cannot read, and his face stays in the shadow of the hood. He stands before you with his arms crossed on his breast in the Sign of Osiris Risen, then lowers them and waits. Greet him in whatever way feels right. Ask plainly: What does this path teach me? Then be still. The answer may come as words, as an image in the smoke of the tripod, as a feeling in the chest, or as a long silence. All of these are acceptable. You may be given a symbol or a word to carry back. Receive whatever comes without interpreting it yet. You may ask one more question. Then thank him and stay quietly in his presence until you are ready to go on.

rows.title: The Threshold of Binah
rows.text: Past the tripod the road climbs, and the orange light cools and thins. The air grows very still, and the wind of the lower path has dropped entirely. The road ends at an edge. Before you lies a great gulf that ordinary sight cannot cross. Stay on this side of it. On the far side, faint and immense, stands a temple of black stone rimmed with dark crimson. Behind it lies a sea without waves, as deep as night. You may sense a vast, patient understanding coming from there, in which the pairs you have just seen do not seem opposed at all. The name Tzaphkiel may come to mind. Do not step forward or try to cross. Look, receive whatever impression comes, and then bow.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Turn and walk back down the path. Pass the tripod and its thread of smoke. As you pass the royal pair beneath the arch of swords, bow to the hooded figure. The roads divide and rejoin under your feet, and the magpie, the orchids and the wind slip by. Ahead you see the two halves of the curtain. Step between them into the golden hall of Tiphareth. Turn to face the veil: the orange letter Zain still hangs before it. Trace it again in reverse and watch it fade until only the painted cloth remains. Turn to Raphael and give thanks for guarding the temple and your way. Let the archangel, the image above the altar and the golden hall fade quietly.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Come back to the body in the chair. Feel your weight, your feet on the floor and, if you are holding it, the stone in your hand. Let the breath become ordinary again, no longer counted, and notice how your two lungs have been working together all this time. Listen to the sounds of the room and beyond it, and notice the smell of the air. Move your fingers and toes and stretch your neck gently. When you are ready, open your eyes, look around and name a few ordinary things you see. Stamp your feet lightly on the floor three times. You are here, in your own time and place.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair with your feet flat on the floor and your hands resting on your thighs. Keep your spine tall but not strained. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let each round be a little slower than the one before. As you breathe, let your attention travel down the body. The scalp softens, the jaw unclenches, the shoulders drop away from the ears, the belly loosens and the legs grow heavy. Notice the weight of the amber in your hand, or its place on the altar before you, and the faint scent of the incense. Let the sounds of the room recede without pushing them away. When the breath has found its own rhythm, rest in it for a while before going on.

rows.title: The Temple of Geburah
rows.text: A five-sided hall forms around you. Its walls are scarlet, the Queen-scale colour of Geburah. The light inside is hot and clear, as if it came from a forge you cannot see. The floor is dark iron and cool under your feet. In the centre stands a plain altar with a sword laid flat on it. Beyond the altar stands the magical image of this sphere, perfectly still: a mighty warrior in a chariot, armed and crowned. Breathe in the dry, sharp air. Now vibrate the God-name, letting it roll from your chest out to all five walls: Elohim Gibor. Feel the hall answer. Call the archangel: Kamael. A tall figure forms in scarlet flecked with green, a sword at rest in its hands. Ask Kamael to guard the temple and your way back.

rows.title: The Veil of the Chariot
rows.text: A heavy curtain hangs in the western wall of the hall. Atu VII, The Chariot, is painted on it: an armoured figure under a deep blue canopy holding a glowing cup, with four strange beasts resting in front of him and scarlet wheels at his sides. Stand in front of the curtain. With your right forefinger, trace the letter Cheth in the air before it in clear amber light. It is two upright strokes joined by a roof across the top, like a gateway or a fenced yard. Vibrate its name: Cheth. The letter hangs there, glowing. The painted cloth ripples as if a tide were moving it, and a gap opens in its centre. Step through and feel the curtain fall closed behind you.

rows.title: The Warded Road
rows.text: You are standing on a road bathed in amber light, warm and dense, like sunlight through resin. Low walls run along both sides, close enough to touch. This is the fence of Cheth, the enclosure that makes a path a path. Beyond the left-hand wall lies a shoreline under a large, pale moon, and the tide draws in and out. At the water's edge a crab moves sideways over the wet stones, carrying its house on its back. A little further on, a turtle rests with its head drawn in. The air smells faintly of the sea and of the incense in your room. Walk slowly. Notice that the walls hold you rather than confine you. Let yourself settle into the pace of the road.

rows.title: The Chariot at Rest
rows.text: The road widens into a courtyard, and the Chariot stands before you. It is not moving. Four sphinxes lie in front of it. Look at each one in turn: every sphinx is made from the same four creatures (bull, lion, eagle and man), combined differently each time. There are no reins. Above the car, four pillars hold up a canopy the deep blue of night, scattered with stars. The wheels are scarlet and still carry the heat of Geburah behind you. The Charioteer sits within, clad in amber armour marked with ten stars. A crab rises from his helm, and his visor is closed, so no face can be seen. In his hands he holds a wide cup of violet stone, and at its centre a light turns slowly, like blood lit from within.

rows.title: The House of Influence
rows.text: Stand quietly near the Chariot and notice what flows here. The old text calls this path the Intelligence of the House of Influence, a place through which abundance passes downward and is received. You may feel it as a gentle pressure from above, as if the night of the canopy were pouring slowly into the cup. At the edge of the courtyard a pool holds a single lotus, still closed at its tip. Beside the pool a black scarab, Khephra, rolls a dark red sun along the ground, pushing it through the night toward a morning you cannot yet see. Somewhere nearby, a furnace glows behind an iron door, and you may feel its warmth in your stomach, the body's own furnace. A piece of amber lies on the ground with something small held unchanged inside it. Look at each image and let it be what it is.

rows.title: The Charioteer Speaks
rows.text: Approach the Chariot and stand in front of the sphinxes. Give whatever sign of respect feels right to you, such as a bow or a hand over the heart. The visor does not open, but you sense attention turning toward you from behind it. Ask plainly: What does this path teach me? Then wait. The answer may come as words from inside the helm, as a picture in the cup, as a feeling in the body, or as nothing at all for a long while. Any of these is acceptable. You may be offered a symbol or a word to carry back. Receive whatever comes without arguing with it or adding to it. If you wish, ask one more question. Then thank the Charioteer and stay silent in his presence until you are ready to go on.

rows.title: The Threshold of Binah
rows.text: Beyond the Chariot the road climbs, and the amber light deepens toward crimson, then toward a darkness that is not empty. The walls of the road end at a ledge. In front of you is a gulf you cannot see across with ordinary sight. Stay on this side of it. Far across it, a temple of black stone rises out of stillness, faintly crimson at its edges. Behind it lies a vast dark sea, completely calm. The shape of the Grail you have just seen echoes that sea. You may sense a great, patient presence, feminine and very old, and the name Tzaphkiel may come to you. Do not step forward and do not try to enter. Simply look, and let whatever you glimpse of Understanding leave its mark on you. Then bow.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Turn and walk back down the road. As you pass the Chariot, bow to the Charioteer. Pass the pool with its lotus, the scarab with its sun and the warm iron door. The walls rise again on either side, and the moonlit shore, the turtle and the crab slide past. Ahead you see the back of the painted curtain. Step through it into the scarlet hall of Geburah. Turn to face the curtain: the amber letter Cheth still hangs there. Trace it again in reverse and watch it fade until only the painted cloth remains. Turn to Kamael and give thanks for guarding the temple and your way. Let the archangel, the image and the hall fade gently into darkness.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Become aware of your body in the chair: its weight, the pressure of your feet on the floor and, if you are holding it, the amber in your hand. Let the breath deepen, then let it become ordinary breathing again, no longer counted. Notice the smell of the room, the sounds outside and the temperature of the air on your skin. Move your fingers and toes and roll your shoulders. When you are ready, open your eyes, look around the room and name a few ordinary objects to yourself. Stamp your feet lightly on the floor three times. You are here, in your own time and place.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright, feet flat on the floor, hands resting open on your thighs. Close your eyes and begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count steady and easy. Let the breath settle into the centre of your chest, and feel your heart beating beneath it, patient and strong. With each exhalation release a little more tension — brow, jaw, throat, shoulders, hands, belly, hips, legs. If restlessness or heat rises in the body, do not suppress it; notice it and let it ride on the breath, the way a rider sits a willing horse. Let the sounds of the room fade into the distance. You are relaxed, awake, and ready.

rows.title: The Temple of Geburah
rows.text: Around you a temple rises: a five-sided hall whose walls burn a deep, clean scarlet, the Queen-scale colour of Geburah. At its heart stands a stone altar, and smoke rises from it with a dry, sharp scent. On the altar lie the implements of this sphere — a sword, a spear, a scourge, and a chain — set out with precision, nothing wasted. Behind the altar, in the red light, stands the image of the sphere: a mighty warrior in a chariot, armed and crowned. Take your place before the altar. Breathe in fully and vibrate the Name so that the walls ring with it: Elohim Gibor. Then call the archangel: Kamael. Sense a stern, upright presence taking its place beside you, clear-eyed and without malice. Ask Kamael to guard your crossing and your return.

rows.title: The Veil of Lust
rows.text: In the wall that faces toward the Pillar of Mercy hangs a curtain painted with Atu XI, Lust, as it appears in the Thoth deck: a woman astride a lion-beast of many heads, leaning back in rapture, lifting high a cup that burns with light. Stand before it and raise your hand. Trace the letter Teth in the air — a rounded form that curls back into itself, like a serpent coiled with its head turned inward. Draw it in clear greenish-yellow light, the King-scale colour of this path, and let it hang there glowing. Vibrate its name: Teth. The letter brightens and seems to breathe; the painted cup catches its light. The curtain draws aside. Step through, carrying Kamael's steadiness at your back.

rows.title: The Level Road
rows.text: You step out onto open land beneath a high, hot sky. This road does not climb; it runs level, straight across the Tree, from the fortress of Severity to the palace of Mercy. The air is full of a greenish-yellow radiance, like midsummer sunlight through young leaves. Golden earth and long grass stretch away on either side, and the ground is warm beneath your feet. Where shadows fall they are tinted deep purple, the Queen-scale colour of the path. Sunflowers stand in rows along the way, their heavy faces turned toward the sun. This is Leo, fixed Fire: heat that does not flicker but endures. Feel it settle into your chest. Your heart beats with it, strong and even, and you walk on at an easy pace.

rows.title: Serpent and Stone
rows.text: A low wall of sun-warmed stone runs beside the road, and set into it, like eyes, are smooth rounded gems across which a single line of light slides as you pass: cat's eye, the stone of this path. You feel watched, though not unkindly. A serpent crosses the road ahead, unhurried, its scales gleaming green-gold, and slips into the grass. Teth is the serpent — coiled, sinuous life that renews itself by shedding its skin. The Sepher Yetzirah names this the Intelligence of the Secret of all Spiritual Activities, the hidden current moving beneath every living impulse. Notice what stirs in your own body as you walk: warmth, desire, eagerness, unease. Treat each as a creature you are coming to know, not an enemy to drive out.

rows.title: The Lion
rows.text: Ahead, on a flat rock in full sun, lies a lion. It is enormous and completely at ease, its mane dark gold, its long tail moving like a serpent. It lifts its head and looks at you. Stay where you are and breathe. Notice what you feel — awe, fear, excitement, the wish to flee or the wish to master it. Do neither. Let your breath slow and your heart open toward the animal as toward a great force of nature that is also part of you. The old lists give this path the power of training wild beasts; it begins here, with unhurried recognition. Courage, on this path, is an open heart in the presence of power. When the lion rises and comes toward you, walk beside it and let it lead.

rows.title: The Woman and the Beast
rows.text: The lion brings you to a place where the road widens into a sun-bright court, and there she waits: a woman, naked and radiant, riding a great beast of many heads, the reins held lightly in one hand, the other lifting a cup that glows red-gold. Her face is full of joy, and nothing in her power is strained. This is the figure of the trump. She may instead appear as a lion-headed goddess, Sekhet or Pasht; accept the form that comes. If you wish to test the vision, trace the letter Teth between you in greenish-yellow light: a true image grows brighter and clearer; if it blurs or coarsens, withdraw with courtesy. If it holds, greet her, ask what this path has to teach you now, and ask for a word, image, or gift to carry back. Then wait in silence and receive whatever comes, without shaping it.

rows.title: The Threshold of Chesed
rows.text: When the exchange is complete, thank her, and thank the lion. The road runs on a little further and ends at a tall doorway in a wall of pale stone. Stand on the threshold and look within, but do not cross. You glimpse the temple of Chesed: a four-square hall of calm, deep blue, the Queen-scale colour, rising to violet in the vaults. After the heat of the plain the air is cool, and it carries the scent of cedar. Far off, a mighty king sits crowned and enthroned, and brilliant beings move about him — the Chashmalim. You may sense the archangel Tzadkiel and hear, faintly, the Name El. Here force is held in generous order; this is the sphere of the Vision of Love. Take in what you are shown, then bow and turn back.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Walk back along the level road, past the sun-bright court, the rock where the lion lay, the wall set with cat's-eye stones, the sunflowers and the warm grass. The greenish-yellow light deepens gradually toward red as the veil of Geburah comes into view. Step through into the five-sided temple. Turn and face the curtain, and see the letter Teth still glowing there. Retrace it in reverse, and watch it sink into the painted card until only the image of Lust remains. The curtain falls still. Turn to Kamael and thank the archangel for keeping watch; feel that stern, clear presence withdraw. Stand a moment in the scarlet hall, upright and whole.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Let the temple of Geburah fade, its red light drawing down into a steady warmth in your chest, and from there into your feet and the floor beneath you. Feel the weight of your body in the chair, your hands on your thighs, your feet on the ground. Take three slow, full breaths. Hear the room around you. Stretch your fingers and toes, roll your neck and shoulders, and open your eyes. Look deliberately at the altar — the candle, the stone, the curling smoke — and name each thing to yourself. If you feel overheated, restless, or elated, sit quietly until it settles. You are fully returned. Reach for your journal before you speak.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright on a firm chair or cushion, spine straight, hands resting on your thighs. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the count become slow and even. With each exhalation, loosen one region of the body in turn — the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs — until the chair is holding you rather than you holding yourself. Feel the length of your back, the column that keeps you upright without strain. Let the sounds of the room recede. Notice the faint scent of narcissus and the single flame before you, then let them sink into the background. You are quiet, alert, and unhurried.

rows.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
rows.text: Around you a temple takes shape: a six-sided hall whose walls glow a warm, clear gold, the Queen-scale colour of Tiphareth. The light seems to come from everywhere at once, as if you stood inside the sun. At the centre stands a cubical altar where olibanum smoulders, and above it hangs a rose-pink radiance, the King-scale colour, like dawn behind the gold. On the eastern wall you see the images of this sphere: a majestic king, a child, a god with arms outstretched upon a cross. Stand before the altar. Draw a full breath and vibrate the Name slowly, letting it resonate through the hall: YHVH Eloah va-Daath. Then call the archangel: Raphael. Feel a presence gather in the east, tall and luminous, carrying the sense of clean moving air and healing. Ask Raphael to watch over your passage and your return.

rows.title: The Veil of the Hermit
rows.text: In the wall that faces toward the Pillar of Mercy, at the top of a few low steps, hangs a heavy curtain painted with Atu IX, The Hermit, as it appears in the Thoth deck: a hooded, cloaked figure bending over a lamp in which a small sun burns, ripe wheat rising around him. Climb the steps and stand before it. Raise your hand and trace the letter Yod in the air — a single small stroke, like a seed or a tongue of flame. Draw it in yellowish-green light, the King-scale colour of the path, and see it hang there, bright and clear. Vibrate its name: Yod. The letter pulses once. The curtain stirs and parts at its centre. Step through, keeping the sense of Raphael's presence behind you.

rows.title: The Road Among the Grain
rows.text: You stand at the foot of a long road that climbs gently away from the sun behind you. The air is filled with a soft yellowish-green light, like new leaves at evening. The ground underfoot is slate-grey stone, cool and dry — the Queen-scale colour of the path — softened here and there by grey-green lichen. On either side lie fields of ripe wheat, heavy-eared and still, for this is Virgo, the harvest sign, earth that has carried its seed to fullness. No wind moves the grain. You are alone, and the solitude feels chosen rather than imposed. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this the Intelligence of Will; here you feel your will not as strain but as quiet direction, like a seed that knows which way is up. Walk slowly, and let your steps set the pace of your breath.

rows.title: Flower, Stone and Hand
rows.text: As the road rises, the fields give way to thin mountain grass. Small white flowers grow along the verge: snowdrops bowing their heads, tall lilies, narcissi whose sweetness is the perfume of this path. Pause and let it reach you. In the grey rock beside you a vein of olive-green crystal catches the light — peridot, the stone of this path. Lay your palm on it and feel its steady coolness. Then look at your own hand. Yod means hand, and this is the path of the hand that holds, withholds, and gives at the right time. Further up, the stone has been worn into shallow steps by those who walked here before you, each of them alone. Ahead, a small cave opens in the hillside, and a faint light glows within.

rows.title: The Terrace of the Egg
rows.text: Before the cave the ground levels into a small terrace, and the design of the trump comes alive around you. On a flat stone rests an egg, pale and smooth, with a serpent coiled about it: the Orphic egg, the world held in potential, life waiting inside its shell. At the edge of the terrace lies a great dog with three heads, calm and watchful, the guardian of the underworld who now follows the one who carries the light. Above, the sky deepens toward twilight and the first stars appear. Let each thing be exactly as it is, and do not force detail. If something appears that you did not expect, note it quietly for later. The silence here is thick and friendly, the silence of someone who has nothing to prove.

rows.title: The Hermit
rows.text: From the mouth of the cave a figure emerges: an ancient one wrapped in a cloak and deep hood, bent a little, carrying a lamp. Inside the lamp burns not a flame but a small, perfect sun — the light of Tiphareth carried inward. The guide may instead come as a silent child with a finger to the lips, Heru-pa-kraath; accept the form that appears. If you wish to test it, trace the Yod between you in yellowish-green light: a true image steadies or brightens; if it blurs or coarsens instead, withdraw with courtesy and return. If it holds, greet the guide and ask plainly what this path has to teach you now, and ask for a word, an image, or a gift to carry back. Then be silent. Whatever comes, or does not come, is yours. Stay with it.

rows.title: The Threshold of Chesed
rows.text: When the meeting is complete, thank your guide. The lamp is lifted toward the summit, and you walk on a little further, to where the road ends at a doorway cut into the rock. Stand on the threshold and look, but do not enter. Beyond lies the temple of Chesed: a four-square hall of deep, calm blue, the Queen-scale colour, shading upward into violet. The air carries the dry, resinous scent of cedar. Far within, a mighty king sits crowned and enthroned, and brilliant presences move around him — the Chashmalim. You may sense the archangel Tzadkiel, and hear the Name El sounding faintly, like a bell across water. This is the sphere of Jupiter, of generous and ordered grace. Take in what you are shown, then bow and turn back.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Walk back down the road the way you came: past the cave and its terrace, the dog and the egg, the vein of peridot, the white flowers, the silent fields of grain. The light warms toward gold as you descend, and ahead the radiance of Tiphareth glows through the curtain. Step through the veil into the six-sided temple. Turn and face the curtain, and see the letter Yod still hanging there. Retrace it in reverse and watch it fade into the cloth until only the painted trump remains. The curtain falls still. Turn to the east, thank Raphael for guarding your passage, and feel the archangel's presence withdraw. Stand a moment in the golden hall, whole and present.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Let the temple of Tiphareth soften and fade, its gold light folding down into a warm point at the centre of your chest. Become aware of your body sitting in the room: the weight of your hands, the contact of your feet with the floor, the length of your back. Take three deliberate, deeper breaths. Hear the ordinary sounds around you. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and when you are ready, open your eyes. Look at the flame, the peridot, the bread on the altar, and name each to yourself. You are fully returned. Before speaking or doing anything else, reach for your journal.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright with your spine straight and your hands resting open on your thighs, palms up. Kaph is the palm, and you begin with it open. Close your eyes. Start the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Notice that the breath is a small wheel, turning through its four quarters without effort once it is set going. With each exhalation loosen something: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. If thoughts rise, let them ride round and drop away like objects carried on a rim. When the rhythm is steady and the body is heavy and at ease, let the outer room recede.

rows.title: The Temple of Netzach
rows.text: You stand in a seven-sided temple of emerald. The walls are green stone veined with paler green, and the light is soft and moving, like sun through leaves. Roses climb the seven pillars, and the air holds benzoin, rose and a trace of red sandalwood. At the centre, on a low altar, burns a single lamp. Beyond it stands the image of this sphere, a beautiful naked woman, calm and unashamed. Face the altar and vibrate the Name so that it rolls around the seven walls: YHVH Tzabaoth. The green deepens and brightens in reply. Then call the archangel: Haniel. A presence gathers in green and rose-coloured light, warm and clear-eyed. Ask Haniel to watch over your going and your return.

rows.title: The Veil of Fortune
rows.text: In the far wall, where a distant blue glimmers through, hangs a curtain. As you approach, its painting comes clear: Atu X, Fortune. A great wheel of ten spokes stands against a violet sky scattered with stars and split by lightning. A Sphinx holding a sword crouches on its rim. One figure climbs up one side while another tumbles down the other. Raise your hand and trace the letter Kaph before the curtain: a stroke across the top that curves round and returns along the base, like a cupped palm: כ. See it shine in clear violet. Vibrate its name: Kaph. The painted wheel gives one slow turn, and the curtain parts at its hub. Step through. The emerald warmth falls behind you, and the air becomes wide and cool.

rows.title: The Open Country
rows.text: You are on a broad road climbing through open country beneath an enormous sky. Overhead the light is violet deepening to royal blue, with bands of gold streaming up from the horizon, so the whole sky seems blue rayed with yellow. The land rolls in long slopes, and there is more room here than you are used to. Great oaks stand alone in the fields, each with space around it. A line of tall poplars marks a far stream, their leaves flickering silver and green. The air smells warm and rich, of saffron and resin. Walk slowly. Notice that the road, though it climbs, bends gently all the while, so that over a long distance you travel around as well as up.

rows.title: Eagle, Fig and Stone
rows.text: An eagle circles high above, riding the warm air in wide rings, rising without a single wingbeat simply by turning. By the roadside grows a fig tree heavy with fruit, and at its roots a low bush of hyssop, blue-flowered and sharply fragrant. Among the roots lie stones: purple amethyst and deep blue lapis flecked with gold. Stoop and rest one in your open palm. Feel its cool weight. Kaph is the palm, the hand that receives and the hand that grasps. Notice which your hand wants to do, then set the stone back. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this road the Intelligence of Conciliation and Reward, the channel that receives the divine influence and passes it on as blessing to all that exists. Let the phrase settle as you walk.

rows.title: The Wheel
rows.text: The road brings you to the foot of a vast wheel standing upright against the sky, its rim taller than any tower, its ten spokes glinting. It turns slowly, and the heavens seem to turn with it: stars wheel past behind it and thin lightning flickers down from above. On one side a jackal-headed figure, Hermanubis, clambers upward on the rim, quick and eager. On the other a dark, heavy figure, Typhon, slides downward, slow and inevitable. At the summit sits the Sphinx, sword in hand, and though the rim moves beneath it, it keeps its place at the top. Stand close and feel the rhythm of the turning in your chest. Then let your attention travel inward along a spoke to the hub, which scarcely moves at all.

rows.title: The Guide: Amoun
rows.text: Beside the axle, where the ground does not move, a tall figure waits. His skin is the blue of lapis and his crown is a pair of tall straight plumes. He holds a long sceptre forked at the foot and topped with an animal's head. This is Amoun-Ra, the Hidden One, whom the Greeks called Zeus Ammon. Approach with open palms. If anything about him feels false, trace Kaph in violet between you. A true figure grows clearer and a false one fades. Greet him and ask what this path has to teach you. Then be quiet and wait. He may speak, point to the wheel, or place something in your hand. Receive whatever comes without shaping it, and remember it.

rows.title: The Threshold of Chesed
rows.text: When the exchange feels complete, thank him in your own way. He lifts the sceptre toward the road that continues beyond the wheel. Follow it a short way uphill until the violet clears into a deep, luminous blue. Ahead stands a four-square temple of blue stone with its doors open, the scent of cedar flowing out. Through the doorway you glimpse a mighty king, crowned and enthroned, in a light that feels generous, orderly and immense. The Name El seems to sound from the stone itself, and Tzadkiel's presence fills the hall. This is Chesed, Mercy, the sphere of Jupiter. Do not enter. Stand on the threshold, let its breadth wash over you like open sky, and take only the impression.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Turn back. Walk down the road, past Amoun beside the axle, past the great wheel still turning with its climber and its faller, past the fig, the hyssop and the stones among the roots.
