The eagle circles overhead as you descend, and the road curves gently beneath your feet. The violet sky softens, and the curtain appears ahead, its painted wheel on this side too. Pass through, then turn to face it. Trace the Kaph once more in violet, and watch the letter sink into the fabric as the curtain seals and stills. You stand again in the seven-sided emerald temple of Netzach, rose scent around you, the lamp burning on the altar. Turn to Haniel, thank the archangel for watching over your journey, and see the presence withdraw into the green light.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Let the green temple dissolve into the darkness behind your eyelids. Feel your body again: the chair beneath you, your feet on the floor, your hands resting palm-up on your thighs. Close your hands gently, so the palm that opened at the start now closes. Take three slower, deeper breaths without counting. Move your fingers and toes, stretch, and open your eyes. Look around the room and name a few plain objects. Press your feet firmly into the floor or stamp them. Then, before anything else, write down what the guide gave you and everything you met on the road: colours, creatures, plants, stones, figures, words. Only afterwards compare them with the symbol list for this path.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the count become even and unforced. With each exhalation release one region of the body: the brow, the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the thighs, the feet. Now notice where you lean. Perhaps more weight sits on one hip, or one side of the neck is tighter than the other. Adjust gently until you feel centred. This path is about balance, and it begins with the body's own. When the breath runs by itself, let the room fade to a quiet background.

rows.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
rows.text: You stand in a six-sided temple of gold. Light comes from everywhere at once, warm and even, like late-morning sun through amber glass. The floor is polished yellow stone, and a banner of deeper gold hangs on each of the six walls. At the centre stands a double-cube altar with a single lamp. Behind it, carved in relief, three images seem to melt into one another as you look: a majestic king, a child, a god with arms stretched upon a cross. A thread of olibanum smoke rises straight up. Face the altar, draw a full breath, and vibrate the Name so it fills the space: YHVH Eloah va-Daath. Feel the gold brighten in answer. Then call the archangel: Raphael. A tall presence gathers beside the altar, robed in gold edged with violet, bringing the smell of clean air. Ask Raphael to guard your going and your return.

rows.title: The Veil of Adjustment
rows.text: In the wall ahead, where a faint red glow shows through from beyond, hangs a heavy curtain. As you approach, its painting sharpens: Atu VIII, Adjustment. A slender masked woman stands poised on the tips of her toes, both hands on the hilt of a long sword pointed down before her, two scale pans hanging from the plumes of her crown. The whole picture is washed in blue and green. Raise your hand and trace the letter Lamed in the air before the curtain, the tall upper stroke first, then the body bending and sweeping down: ל. See it burn in clear emerald green. Vibrate its name: Lamed. The letter flares, and the curtain parts along the line of the painted sword. Step through. The gold falls away behind you, and cool green air touches your face.

rows.title: The Level Road
rows.text: You stand on a straight road of pale stone running gently uphill, perfectly level from side to side. On either hand stretches a plain of emerald grass, so even it might have been cut with one stroke. The sky is a deep blue-green, like sea over white sand, and the light is cool and steady, casting short, clean shadows. Nothing leans here. The few trees stand plumb, and the grass tilts neither way. A sharp, green, resinous scent hangs in the air: galbanum. As you walk, notice your own gait. Where you favour one leg, the road seems to rise a little on that side. When you correct yourself, it lies flat again. Walk on until your steps fall evenly, left and right, each the same length and the same weight.

rows.title: Goad, Elephant and Aloe
rows.text: Ahead, an elephant stands across the road, grey and patient, its trunk swinging slowly. It is so heavy the ground ought to tilt beneath it, yet everything stays level. As you come near it steps aside. Where it stood grows a clump of aloe, thick-leaved, a broken tip beading with bitter, healing sap. Beside the aloe lies a long staff with an iron point: an ox-goad. Pick it up and feel its weight. It is not a weapon but a prompt, the small sharp touch that keeps a strong beast moving along its furrow. Lamed is this goad, and Aleph, the ox, is what it drives. Together they spell AL. Lay the goad back where you found it. Recall that the Sepher Yetzirah names this the Faithful Intelligence, by which spiritual virtues are increased.

rows.title: The Balance
rows.text: The road opens into a round court paved in squares of pale green and deep blue. In its centre hangs a great balance, its beam as long as a ship, its chains rising out of sight into the blue-green sky. In one pan rests an Alpha, in the other an Omega, both cut from emerald, and the beam is perfectly still. Set into the paving beneath it is an equal-armed cross. At the edges of the court rest four spheres, two bright and two dark, holding one another in equilibrium. This is Libra, cardinal Air, the equinox where day and night are equal. Stand beneath the beam and recall one recent action of your own. Let it be weighed: what led to it, and what followed. Do not judge it. Simply watch the pans register it and come to rest.

rows.title: The Guide: Maat
rows.text: Beyond the balance, on a low dais, you see her: the woman of the trump, tall and slender, masked, balanced on the very tips of her toes. The ostrich plumes of Maat rise from her head, and from them hang the scales. Both her hands rest on the hilt of the great sword, its point touching the ground between her feet. She seems utterly still, yet you sense constant, minute motion, as if she corrects for every tremor in the world. If anything about her feels false, trace Lamed in emerald between you. A true figure grows clearer and a false one fades. Greet her as Maat and ask what this path has to teach you. Then wait. She may speak, show you something, or place something in your hands. Receive it without shaping it, and remember it.

rows.title: The Threshold of Geburah
rows.text: When the exchange feels complete, thank her. She turns her masked face slightly toward the road beyond. Follow it a short way to where the green light warms through orange into scarlet. Ahead rises a five-sided temple of red stone with its doors open. Through them you glimpse a mighty warrior in his chariot, armed and crowned, and feel a dry heat like a forge. A strong scent of tobacco leaf drifts out. The Name Elohim Gibor hangs in the air, and within is the presence of Kamael. This is Geburah, Severity, the sphere of Mars, home of the sword you have just seen held so carefully. Do not enter. Stand on the threshold, let the force touch your face like warmth from a fire, and take only the impression.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Now turn around. Walk back down the road, past the woman with the sword, across the chequered court beneath the still balance, past the aloe and the place where the elephant stood. Keep your steps even. The emerald plain and the blue-green sky carry you gently downward. Soon the curtain appears, painted on this side with the same trump. Pass through it, then turn and face it. Trace the Lamed once more in emerald green, and watch the letter sink into the fabric as the curtain falls closed and still. You stand again in the gold temple of Tiphareth, olibanum in the air, the lamp burning on the altar. Turn to Raphael and thank the archangel for guarding the way. See the presence withdraw into the light.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Let the golden temple fade, like sunlight seen through closed eyelids. Become aware of your body in the chair: its weight, the floor under your feet, the air on your hands and face. Take three slow, deeper breaths and let the fourfold count go. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and when you are ready, open your eyes. Look around the room and name a few ordinary things you can see. Stamp your feet lightly or press your palms flat against the floor. Before doing anything else, write down what the guide said or showed you, and every colour, animal, object and word you met. Only then compare your notes with the symbol list for this path.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright with your spine straight, feet flat on the floor and hands resting palms-down on your thighs. Close your eyes and begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold full for four, out for four, hold empty for four. After several rounds let the count grow soft and automatic. Now relax the body in stages, following the breath downward: forehead and eyes, jaw and tongue, throat, shoulders, arms, chest, belly, hips, legs and feet. Imagine the body slowly filling with still, cool water, rising from the soles to the crown until nothing in you moves except the breath. Let thoughts pass like reflections on the surface. When you feel quiet and heavy, notice a warm orange glow beginning in the darkness in front of you.

rows.title: The Temple of Hod
rows.text: The orange glow resolves into walls. You stand in an eight-sided temple of clear, bright orange. The floor is laid in black and white squares, and the air is sweet with the balsam of storax. On the central altar lie a caduceus and a shallow dish of quicksilver that trembles and shines at the smallest movement. Shelves of books and scrolls line the walls. At the far side stands the magical image of this sphere: a hermaphrodite, poised and composed, holding both natures without strain. Stand before the altar and vibrate the God-name of Hod, Elohim Tzabaoth, and feel the sound fill all eight walls. Then call the archangel: Mikael. Wait until you sense a tall, alert presence beside you, bright as polished metal, and ask Mikael to guard the way you are about to take.

rows.title: The Veil of Mem
rows.text: Turn to the wall through which the path rises, straight up the pillar toward Geburah. A curtain hangs there, painted with Atu XII: a man hanging head-downward from an ankh, legs crossed, arms spread, against a grid of green tablets above dark water. Look at it until the image is clear and steady. Raise your hand and trace the letter Mem, מ, on the curtain stroke by stroke in deep blue light. Vibrate its name: Mem. Let your lips close on the final M and become a hum that fills your skull and chest; the Sepher Yetzirah calls Mem the humming letter, the mother of Water. The letter glows deep and steady, the painted water seems to ripple, and the curtain parts. Glance back at Mikael, then step through.

rows.title: The Causeway
rows.text: You stand at the edge of water. A great still lake, or a windless sea, stretches ahead under a deep blue sky. The path runs straight out across it as a narrow causeway of sea-green stone, level with the surface. Near your feet the water is clear. Farther out it darkens to deep olive-green and then to depths you cannot see. The cool air smells of myrrh and of something older and sharper, like shell and resin: onycha. Lotus flowers rest on the surface in scattered clusters, white flecked with purple, their stems going down out of sight. Begin to walk. Your footsteps make no echo. The stillness is not empty; it is the stillness of something very large holding its breath. Let your own breath slow to match it.

rows.title: The Hanged Man
rows.text: Midway across, the causeway ends at a tall ankh of pale stone rising from the water, its loop dark against the sky. A man hangs from it by one foot, head downward, just above the surface. His free leg crosses behind the other, so his legs form a cross. His arms spread outward and down, so that together with his head they form a triangle pointing at the water. Flat green tablets stand behind him in a grid, and you can see where he is nailed to them, yet his face is calm and his eyes are open. Beneath his shaven head, in the darker water, a serpent lies coiled and quiet. Stand before him. Notice any urge to rescue him, or to look away. Neither is needed. Simply watch how completely he is held.

rows.title: The Stable Intelligence
rows.text: Walk slowly around the ankh. Now and then the surface stirs: pale shapes of nymphs and undines rise, look at you without speaking, and sink again. Far overhead an eagle circles. On the stone at the foot of the ankh a scorpion rests, and below it the serpent turns its head. Eagle, snake and scorpion together are the Kerub of Water. Set into the stone is a beryl, clear sea-green, like a drop of this water made solid. Lay your hand on it. Feel that nothing here wobbles; even the hanging man is held in perfect balance. This is the Stable Intelligence, the constancy that runs through all the spheres and keeps each true to itself. Notice a quiet settling in your belly, in the organs of nourishment, as if something long clenched in you were finally allowed to rest and be fed.

rows.title: Asar
rows.text: Go back and stand before the hanging figure. You may know him now by an older name: Asar, Osiris, the god given to the waters who does not stay lost in them. He turns his calm, inverted gaze to you. Greet him. If you wish to test the vision, trace Mem before him in deep blue light; a true guide stays steady in it. A cup stands on the stone at the foot of the ankh, and if it is offered, you may drink. Then ask him what this path has to teach you, and what in you needs to be turned upside down. Wait. Let the answer come in whatever form it takes: a word, an image, a sensation, a change in how you see him or yourself, or silence. If you feel drawn to, you may share his view for a while, the world hanging from the water, but do not force anything. Take the time you need.

rows.title: The Threshold of Geburah
rows.text: When the exchange feels complete, thank him. Beyond the ankh the causeway continues, and now it begins to climb out of the water, rising straight ahead. Walk until the air grows warmer and drier and the blue sky takes on an edge of orange. The path ends at a threshold of red stone. Beyond it you glimpse the fifth sphere: a five-sided hall of scarlet, lit by a fierce, clean light. You may hear iron ringing and wheels turning, see a mighty warrior in his chariot, armed and crowned, and smell tobacco smoke on the hot air. Do not cross. Stand at the threshold and notice how the calm you carry from the water meets that force.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Turn and walk back along the causeway. The air cools, and the path sinks until it runs level with the still surface again. Pass the ankh and the hanging man, and bow to him as you go. Pass the lotus flowers, white flecked with purple. Keep the word or symbol you received safe. The curtain appears ahead with the deep blue Mem still shining on it. Step through into the orange temple of Hod. Turn to face the curtain and trace the letter in reverse, drawing it back until it fades and the painted card grows still. Turn to Mikael and thank the archangel for guarding the way. Let the eight walls soften into orange light, and the light into darkness.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Let the water you imagined filling your body drain slowly downward, through your legs and feet into the floor, and leave the body its ordinary weight and warmth. Take a few rounds of the fourfold breath, then let the breath return to its natural rhythm. Feel the seat beneath you, the floor under your feet, the air on your skin. Listen to the sounds of the room and of the world beyond it. Move your fingers and toes, and stretch your neck and shoulders. Say your name, the date and where you are. Open your eyes and look at a few ordinary objects, naming each one. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor. You are back, fully present, and the path is closed.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair or on a cushion with your spine straight and your hands resting on your thighs, and close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold full for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count slow and even for several rounds until it runs by itself. On each exhalation let one part of the body let go: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the chest, the belly, the legs, the feet. Feel your weight settle into the seat and the floor. Let the sounds of the room fade without pushing them away. When the body is heavy and quiet and the breath is steady, notice a faint green light starting to gather in the darkness in front of you.

rows.title: The Temple of Netzach
rows.text: The green light widens into a room. You stand in a seven-sided temple whose walls glow a deep, luminous emerald. The floor is cool under your bare feet, and the warm air carries benzoin, rose and red sandalwood. At the centre stands a double-cube altar draped in green, with a single lamp and a bowl of red roses on it. Behind the altar, in a niche, stands the magical image of this sphere: a beautiful naked woman, calm and unashamed. Take a full breath and vibrate the God-name of Netzach, YHVH Tzabaoth, and let it resound from all seven walls. Then call the archangel: Haniel. Wait, and feel a presence gather beside you, tall and bright, in green and rose light. Ask Haniel to watch over the way you are about to take.

rows.title: The Veil of Nun
rows.text: Turn to the wall that faces inward, toward the centre of the Tree. A heavy curtain hangs there, painted with Atu XIII: a crowned skeleton sweeping its scythe through a dark, curling sea of forms. Look at it until the picture holds steady. Then raise your hand and trace the letter Nun, נ, on the curtain in clear green-blue light: the small head, the long downward stroke, the short base turning to the left. Vibrate its name, Nun, and let the sound hum in your chest. The letter brightens, the painted figures seem to stir, and the curtain parts down its centre. Glance back once at Haniel, then step through.

rows.title: The River of the Fish
rows.text: You stand at the foot of a long slope that rises gently ahead under a sky of deep green-blue, the colour of water seen from below. The ground is soft, dull brown earth, damp and rich, smelling of leaf-mould and of the dark, sweet resin of opoponax. A slow river runs beside the path and catches the green-blue light. In its shallows fish are moving, silver shapes turning in the current and working their way upstream, the same way you are going. Cactus and nettle grow along the bank, so walk with your hands at your sides. The air is still and faintly warm, with the warmth of fallen things quietly turning into soil. Begin to walk, and let each step settle into the earth. Nothing on this path hurries. It moves at the pace of decay and growth.

rows.title: The Dancer with the Scythe
rows.text: Ahead, where the path opens into a low meadow, a figure is at work. It is a skeleton, tall and unhurried, wearing the tall plumed crown of Osiris. It swings a great scythe in wide, even arcs, and it is dancing rather than labouring. Where the blade passes, the air curls into dark waves, and bubbles rise in the waves, each holding a small form: a seed, an embryo, a face not yet decided. What the scythe cuts, it also sets moving. At its feet a scorpion rests on a flat stone, a serpent raises its head beside it, and a fish leaps at the river's edge. High above, an eagle turns slowly against the green-blue sky. Stand and watch the rhythm of the blade until it feels less like a threat and more like a pulse.

rows.title: The Imaginative Intelligence
rows.text: The skeleton lets you pass, and the path climbs on beside the river. As you walk, a slow warmth gathers low in your belly, as though your gut were at last digesting something held for a long time. This path rules the intestines, where what is taken in is broken down so it can become you. In the bank lies a coiled fossil shell, a snakestone, beside a chip of greenish turquoise. Pick up the fossil: a living creature, long gone, turned into pattern. This is the Imaginative Intelligence, which gives things their likeness and carries a form's image forward after the form itself is spent. Let something you have outgrown or lost rise gently in memory, and notice what of it stays with you as shape and meaning. Set the stone down. A black beetle with a dark indigo-brown shell crosses in front of you, pushing a small ball of earth. Follow it.

rows.title: Khephra
rows.text: The beetle leads you to a bend in the river where the light begins, very faintly, to warm. There, seated on a rock, is a figure with a man's body and a great scarab in place of a head. This is Khephra, who rolls the sun through the hours of night toward its rising. He holds the ball of earth the beetle brought, and now you see a faint light glowing inside it. Greet him with respect. If you wish to test the vision, trace the letter Nun before him in green-blue light; a true guide stays steady in it. Ask him plainly what this path has to teach you, and what in you is ready to die. Then be silent. Let whatever comes arise in its own way: an image, a word, a feeling, something placed in your hands, or nothing at all. Do not reach for an answer or decide in advance what it should be. Take the time you need.

rows.title: Before Paroketh
rows.text: When the exchange is complete, thank Khephra and take your leave. Walk on up the slope until the path meets a curtain of fine mist, rose-pink and gold, hanging across the way. This is Paroketh, the veil before the sphere of the Adepts. Stop here. Through it you glimpse the sixth sphere: a vast golden radiance, warm on your face like noon, with the outline of a six-sided hall inside it. You may sense the images of Tiphareth, a king in majesty, a child, a figure with arms outstretched, and smell olibanum drifting toward you. Do not cross. It is enough to stand before the veil, let its light fall on you, and feel how naturally this path leads here.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Turn and walk back down the path. Pass the bend of the river and the stones on the bank, then the meadow where the scythe still swings in its slow dance. The fish still turn in the shallows. Keep the word or symbol you were given close to you. Soon the curtain appears ahead, with the green-blue letter Nun still glowing on it. Step through into the emerald temple of Netzach. Turn to face the curtain and trace the letter in reverse, drawing it back until it fades and the painted card grows still. Turn to Haniel and thank the archangel for guarding the way. Watch the green light soften as the temple gently fades around you.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Let the temple dissolve into a soft green glow, and the glow into the ordinary darkness behind your eyelids. Return to the fourfold breath for a few rounds, then let the breath find its natural rhythm. Feel the weight of your body on the seat, the pressure of your feet on the floor, the temperature of the air on your hands and face. Listen to the sounds of the room. Move your fingers and toes, and roll your shoulders. Quietly say your own name, the date and where you are. When you are ready, open your eyes and look around, naming a few objects you see. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor. You are here, in your body and in the present, and the path is closed behind you.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright with your spine straight and your feet flat, hands resting palms-down on your thighs. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold full for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the counting slow and unforced. As you breathe, move your attention down through the body, releasing tension wherever you find it: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. Feel yourself grow heavy and still, your spine rising in a straight line from the seat to the crown. Keep breathing until the breath settles into an even rhythm on its own, then let the counting go and rest.

rows.title: The Temple of Yesod
rows.text: Build the temple of Yesod around you. It has nine sides, and its walls glow a soft violet, the Queen-scale colour of the Foundation. Moonlight falls through an opening in the roof onto a round, still pool at the centre, and the air smells sweet with jasmine. Beside the pool stands the magical image of this sphere: a beautiful naked man, very strong, standing at ease, his strength quiet and complete. Everything in this temple shimmers slightly, the way images do before they settle into form. Breathe in, and vibrate the God-name so that it fills all nine walls: Shaddai El Chai. Then call the archangel of Yesod: Gabriel. Feel a presence gather above the water, cool and clear, robed in silver and blue, holding a cup.

rows.title: The Veil of Samekh
rows.text: A curtain hangs in the wall that leads straight upward along the Middle Pillar. It is painted with Atu XIV, Art: a single two-faced figure pouring fire and water into a golden cauldron, with a lion and an eagle at its feet. Stand before it and trace the letter Samekh in the air in clear, bright blue: ס. Watch the rounded letter close on itself and shine against the cloth. Vibrate its name, letting the sound rise through your body: Samekh. The letter glows, the painted figure seems to breathe, and the curtain parts. As you step through, look back. Above the temple of Yesod a great rainbow arcs across the sky like a drawn bow, and you are the arrow set to its string. Gabriel stays at the threshold. Let the curtain close behind you.

rows.title: The Straight Road
rows.text: You stand at the start of a road that runs ahead without a single bend, climbing gently toward a point of light on the far horizon. The sky is a deep, clear blue, and the plain on either side is green with grass. A stream runs beside the road, thick with rushes whose tall stems rustle in the wind. The air is warm and dry and smells of resinous, woody aloes. This is Sagittarius, mutable Fire ruled by Jupiter. The land is open and wide, and the horizon seems to pull you forward. Begin to walk. Feel the strength in your hips and thighs and the long, easy stride. The road never turns, so your only task is to keep your eyes on the light ahead.

rows.title: Centaur, Arrow and Desert
rows.text: You hear hooves behind you. Horses stream across the plain, manes flying, and a lean hunting dog falls in at your side, matching your pace. Then a centaur draws alongside: a man's torso rising from the powerful body of a horse, a bow across his back. He holds out a single arrow and lets you take it. Feel its weight and its perfect straightness. Its head is a deep orange-red stone, a jacinth, holding the light. Then he wheels away, and the horses and the dog go with him. The green plain thins into pale, open desert. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this the Intelligence of Probation, the place of testing. Nothing dramatic happens here. There is only distance, silence, and the question of whether you will keep walking. Keep walking, the arrow in your hand.

rows.title: The Cauldron of Art
rows.text: At the heart of the desert, in a circle of warm light, the figure of the trump waits. It is one being with two faces, one pale and one dark: the royal couple of the Lovers made one. A stream of fire falls from a torch in one hand, and water pours from a cup in the other. Both fall into a golden cauldron. Where they meet they neither put each other out nor scald each other, but rise together as a glowing vapour. A white lion and a red eagle flank the cauldron, their colours swapped from the Lovers card. A raven perches on a skull on the cauldron. Around the figure, in a disc of light, runs the Latin motto Visita Interiora Terrae Rectificando Invenies Occultum Lapidem: visit the interior of the earth; by rectifying you will find the hidden stone. As you watch, the vapour shimmers with every colour of a peacock's tail. Stand and watch the work.

rows.title: The Figure of Art
rows.text: The figure turns from the cauldron and looks at you with both faces at once. It may also appear as a huntress with a drawn bow, Diana or Artemis, as the old attributions allow. Accept whichever form comes. Greet it, and hold out the arrow the centaur gave you. Ask what this path has to teach you, and what in you needs to be tempered. Then wait in silence. The answer may come as words, as an image in the cauldron's vapour, as a feeling in the body, or as a symbol placed in your hands. It may be very simple. Don't hurry it or shape it. Stay with the figure and whatever comes up, for as long as it lasts.

rows.title: The Threshold of Tiphareth
rows.text: When the exchange is complete, the figure takes your arrow, sets it to a bow and looses it straight up the road. Follow its flight with your eyes, then with your feet. The desert ends at a curtain of shimmering light, the Veil of Paroketh, with a great golden sun blazing through it. Beyond the veil you see a six-sided temple of clear gold, filled with a warm, rosy light, and at its centre your arrow has struck home. Within the brightness you may sense a king, a child, a god offered up. The air is rich with frankincense. Do not cross the veil. Stand at its edge, take in the warmth on your face and chest, and know that this is where the arrow was always pointed. Then lower your eyes.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Turn and go back down the straight road. Thank the figure of Art as you pass the cauldron. Cross the desert, which feels shorter now, and come back to the green plain, the rushes by the stream and the blue sky. The centaur and the dog may greet you as you pass. Ahead you see the painted curtain beneath the arc of the rainbow. Step through into the violet temple of Yesod. Turn and trace the letter Samekh once more in blue over the curtain, then watch it fade and the curtain become solid wall. Stand by the moonlit pool. Thank Gabriel for keeping the threshold, and let the God-name Shaddai El Chai sound once, softly, in your mind.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Let the nine violet walls grow faint and the moonlight fade until only your ordinary sense of the room is left. Feel the chair beneath you, the floor under your feet, the temperature of the air on your skin. Take three slow, full breaths, each one bringing you further back into your body. Notice the sounds around you. Move your fingers and toes, stretch your arms and gently roll your neck. When you are ready, open your eyes and let them rest on something solid and ordinary. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor two or three times, and pat your arms and legs. You are fully here.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat and hands resting on your thighs, or take the god-form posture if you know it. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count slow and even. With each out-breath, let one part of the body let go: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs. Notice your weight settling down into the seat and the floor. Thoughts will pass. Let them go by like traffic heard through a closed window. When the breath keeps its rhythm without effort, stop counting and rest in it for a while.

rows.title: The Temple of Hod
rows.text: A temple forms around you. It has eight sides, and its walls glow a clear, warm orange, the Queen-scale colour of Hod. The floor is laid in black and white squares, and the air smells of sweet storax resin. An altar stands at the centre. Above it hangs the magical image of this sphere, poised and calm: a hermaphrodite, holding both halves of the self in balance. Faint symbols and figures move across the walls like writing that keeps rearranging itself. This is Mercury's splendour, the mind's delight in order and pattern. Breathe in, and vibrate the God-name so that it resonates through the whole temple: Elohim Tzabaoth. Then call the archangel of Hod: Mikael. Feel a tall, bright presence gather in the orange light behind you. Mikael keeps both the way out and the way home.

rows.title: The Veil of Ayin
rows.text: A heavy curtain hangs in the wall that faces the heart of the Tree. It is painted with Atu XV of the Thoth deck: the great goat with spiralling horns and an eye in his forehead, standing on a mountaintop in front of a towering column. Stand before the curtain. With your finger or wand, trace the letter Ayin in the air in front of the painting, in a deep indigo light that glows against the fabric: ע. Vibrate its name slowly and feel it resonate in your chest: Ayin. The letter holds steady, and the painted goat seems to look back at you. The curtain grows thin, then parts. Mikael puts a small lit lamp in your hand. Step through, and let the curtain fall closed behind you.

rows.title: The Mountain Track
rows.text: You stand at the foot of a mountain in the last hour before full night. The sky is indigo, darkening to black at its edges, and the rock under your feet is a cold dark grey, almost black. The air is thin and sharp with frost, with a faint smell of musk. A narrow track zigzags upward between boulders. Your lamp throws a small warm circle ahead of you, enough for the next few steps and no more. Begin to climb. This is Capricorn, cardinal Earth ruled by Saturn. The going is slow and steady, and it asks for patience, not haste. Feel the effort in your thighs and knees, the grit shifting under your feet, your breath clouding in the lamplight. Every step lands on solid ground.

rows.title: Goat, Ass and Black Diamond
rows.text: Thistles grow in the cracks along the track, their purple heads closed against the cold. Among them you may notice other hardy plants: the ragged leaves of hemp, the pale root of an orchis pushing through thin soil. A laden ass comes plodding down the slope, patient under its load, and you step aside to let it pass. Higher up, goats move with perfect ease along ledges that look impossible, leaping from rock to rock. One stops and looks down at you. Hold its gaze. Its pupil is a flat horizontal bar, strange and steady. This is the Eye, the meaning of Ayin: seeing the world from an angle that is not your own. Where your lamplight touches a seam in the rock, something flashes. It is a black diamond set in the stone, dark and full of fire. Look at it for as long as you need.

rows.title: The Lord of the Gates of Matter
rows.text: The track brings you out onto the summit. On the highest rock stands the figure of the trump: a great Himalayan goat, his horns turning in slow spirals, a third eye open in the middle of his forehead. He is grinning, but the grin is not cruel. It is the pleasure of a creature as much at home on barren stone as in any green valley. Behind him a huge column rises from the mountain into the sky. At its root, two translucent globes hold small figures that stir and press against the walls, like seeds about to break open. In front of him rises a wand topped with a winged disc and twin serpents. The Sepher Yetzirah names this path the Renovating Intelligence. Breathe the thin, clear air and let it renew you. Stand in the presence of this force and simply watch.

rows.title: Pan
rows.text: Near the summit, in the shelter of a boulder, someone is waiting: a figure with the horns and legs of a goat and the body and face of a man. This is Pan, whose name the Greeks heard as 'All'. He may be playing a reed pipe, or just sitting with his arms around his knees, watching you with amusement. Greet him politely, and ask him plainly what this path has to teach you. Then wait. He may answer in words, with a gesture or a sound, with laughter, or by showing you something. He may give you a symbol or a single word. Take whatever comes without judging it, and don't decide yet what it means. If nothing seems to come, that is also an answer. Stay with him in the silence.

rows.title: The Threshold of Tiphareth
rows.text: When the exchange feels complete, Pan points onward. Past the summit the path narrows to a ridge, and at its end the dark gives way to a wash of rose and gold, as if dawn were breaking from inside the rock. Walk to the edge of that light and stop. Across a shimmering veil, the Veil of Paroketh, you see a six-sided temple of gold, bright as the midday sun. Inside it you may make out the shapes of a king, a child, a god offered up. Feel the warmth on your face and smell the frankincense drifting toward you. Do not cross. This is Tiphareth, Beauty, the heart of the Tree. It is enough to know it is there and that this path leads to it. Let the light print itself on you, then lower your eyes.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Turn and retrace your steps. Cross back over the summit, bowing your head in thanks to Pan and the great goat as you go. Go down the zigzag track by the light of your lamp, past the goats on their ledges, the black diamond in the rock, the thistles closed against the cold. Going down is quicker and lighter than the climb. At the foot of the mountain the painted curtain is waiting. Pass through it into the orange temple of Hod. Turn back and trace the letter Ayin once more in indigo over the curtain, then watch the letter fade and the curtain become solid wall. Give the lamp back to Mikael and thank the archangel for guarding the way. Stand for a moment in the warm splendour of the eight-sided temple.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Let the temple of Hod grow faint, its orange walls fading into your ordinary awareness of the room. Feel your body again: the weight of your seat, the soles of your feet on the floor, the air on your hands and face. Take three deeper, fuller breaths, each one bringing you further back. Listen to the sounds of the room and the world outside it. Wriggle your fingers and toes and roll your shoulders. When you are ready, open your eyes. Look around and name a few ordinary objects to yourself. Before you do anything else, stamp your feet firmly on the ground and sit quietly a moment longer. You have returned.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a straight-backed chair with your feet flat on the floor and your hands resting palm-down on your thighs. Let your spine lengthen and your chin drop slightly. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: breathe in for four slow counts, hold for four, breathe out for four, hold empty for four. After a few rounds, use each out-breath to release tension from one part of the body at a time: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, arms, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. Watch especially for clenching in the jaw and fists, and let it go. When the body feels settled and heavy, stop counting and let the breath find its own rhythm. Rest there for a while, awake and still.

rows.title: The Temple of Hod
rows.text: An eight-sided temple forms around you. Its walls are a clear, warm orange, and the light is bright and even, like afternoon sun through amber glass. The floor is polished stone laid in a precise geometric pattern. The air is sweet and faintly balsamic with storax. At the centre stands a double-cube altar draped in orange, with a single flame on it and beside it a caduceus, the sign of Mercury, whose sphere this is. Near the altar stands the image of Hod: a hermaphrodite, poised and composed, both and neither. Take your place before the altar, facing east. Breathe deeply and vibrate the divine name of this sphere so that the eight walls ring with it: Elohim Tzabaoth.

rows.title: Calling Mikael
rows.text: Call on the archangel of Hod: 'Mikael, archangel of this sphere, be present and protect this working.' The orange light behind the altar gathers and brightens until a tall presence stands there, armoured or robed, with a clear and searching quality like light off polished metal. Around the walls you may sense the Beni Elohim, the Sons of the Gods and the choir of this sphere, as a quick shimmer at the edges of your vision. Tell Mikael that you mean to walk the path of Pe across to Netzach and to return by the same road. Wait until you feel you have been heard. Then look to the wall on your right, where a curtain hangs, glowing deep scarlet.

rows.title: The Veil of Pe
rows.text: Walk to the curtain. It is painted with Atu XVI, The Tower, in Crowley and Harris's design. A rigid tower breaks apart under a forked bolt, flames burst from gaping jaws at its base, stiff geometric figures tumble from its walls, and a single radiant eye looks down over it all. Hold the image until it is vivid. Then, with the index finger of your right hand, trace the letter Pe, פ, on the curtain in brilliant scarlet, the King-scale colour of this path. Let it burn there, bright as a live coal. Breathe in fully and vibrate the name of the letter: Pe (peh). The sound seems to strike the curtain like a blow, and it splits open from top to bottom. Step through, and feel it close behind you.

rows.title: The Red Plain
rows.text: You stand at the edge of a wide plain under a heavy, low sky. The light is scarlet, and the earth under your feet is red, dense and faintly springy, as though the ground itself were muscle. The air is hot and carries a peppery, resinous sharpness you can taste at the back of your throat. Behind you the orange light of Hod glows faintly; far across the plain a green gleam marks where the road ends. Clumps of bitter grey-green absinthe and rue grow along the way. Begin to walk. Feel your own strength in each step as the muscles of your legs, back and arms work together. This is the Exciting Intelligence, the path by which every created thing receives its spirit and its motion. Let that energy rise in you, steady and warm, without urgency.

rows.title: The Creatures of Mars
rows.text: As you walk, the plain comes alive. A red-brown horse gallops past in the distance, gleaming, then wheels away. On a low ridge a bear rears up, drops, and ambles on. At the edge of your sight a grey wolf keeps pace with you, silent, neither threatening nor friendly. Somewhere in the scrub a boar crashes through the undergrowth. Let each creature be exactly as it appears, and notice your own response to it: fear, excitement, admiration, calm. Midway across the plain another road crosses yours at right angles, running from the lunar lowlands up toward a golden height. This is the path of Samekh. You do not turn onto it. Ahead, rising out of the flat land, you now see a tall, angular building. It is the Tower.

rows.title: The Lightning
rows.text: Stop at a safe distance and watch. The tower is severe and angular, built of hard, square-cut blocks, its walls without ornament. Above it, in the darkening sky, an immense eye opens, rayed with light. In that instant forked lightning strikes the summit. The structure splits and blocks shear away. Stiff geometric figures, more like broken diagrams than people, tumble from its walls. At its base great jaws gape and breathe out fire. Through the smoke a white dove flies with an olive sprig in its beak, and near it a lion-headed serpent coils in the air; Crowley read the two as two forms of desire. You are not harmed. Watch until the tower is down. Then quietly ask yourself what in you resembles that tower, and simply notice what comes.

rows.title: The Falcon-Headed Warrior
rows.text: Where the tower stood, the air begins to clear. Out of the settling dust walks a warrior with the head of a falcon. He may be Horus in his martial aspect, whom 777 gives to this path, or Menthu, the war-god of Thebes, crowned with tall plumes and a disc; accept whichever form appears. He carries a sword, and his presence is hot, direct and unhurried. Salute him in your own way. Tell him you have come from Hod by the path of Pe, and ask: what does this path have to teach me? Then be still and wait. The answer may come as a spoken word, a gesture, an image, a sensation in the body, or something placed in your hands. Receive it as it is, without editing it. Take all the time you need, and when it feels complete, thank him.

rows.title: The Threshold of Netzach
rows.text: Walk on across the last of the plain. The scarlet light cools and softens, and green enters it. Grass grows under your feet, and the peppery air gives way to the scent of roses and red sandalwood. You come to a threshold and stop. Beyond it stands a seven-sided temple of glowing emerald, its outline lit amber, and above it the planet Venus shines clear. Through the open door you may glimpse the image of this sphere, a beautiful naked woman, and faintly hear the name YHVH Tzabaoth. Do not cross. Stand at the edge and feel the contrast between the road of breaking behind you and the beauty before you. Let the vision of Victory rest in you for a few breaths.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Turn and walk back across the plain the way you came. Pass the place where the tower stood; see what remains there now, and note it without stopping. Salute the falcon-headed warrior if he is still present. Cross the road of Samekh again, and pass the horse, the watchful wolf, the absinthe and rue. The light deepens to scarlet, and then the orange glow of Hod appears ahead. The curtain stands before you; step through into the eight-sided temple. Turn and see the letter Pe still burning on the curtain. Trace it in reverse, or draw your hand down through it, and watch the scarlet fade until the curtain hangs plain and closed. Face the altar and thank Mikael for his protection. Vibrate once more: Elohim Tzabaoth.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Let the temple of Hod fade. The orange walls, the altar flame and the patterned floor dissolve like a picture in dimming light. Feel your body in the chair again: the weight of your hips, your feet on the floor, your hands on your thighs. Take three fuller breaths, and with each one feel your body grow more solid and present. Listen to the ordinary sounds of the room. Press your feet firmly into the floor, open and close your hands, and stretch your arms. When you are ready, open your eyes and look slowly around at familiar things. Say your name aloud. Sit for a moment longer, then write down everything you experienced, starting with whatever the warrior gave you.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair with your feet flat on the floor, your hands resting on your thighs and your spine tall without strain. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count slow and even. With each out-breath, let one part of the body soften in turn: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs, the feet. Notice the weight of your body resting on the chair and the floor. When thoughts arrive, let them drift across your attention and return to the count. Continue until the breath runs on by itself and the body feels heavy, warm and still. Then let the counting fall away and simply rest in the quiet.

rows.title: The Temple of Yesod
rows.text: Around you a temple takes shape. It has nine walls of deep, glowing violet, a floor dark and smooth as still water, and cool air sweet with jasmine. Through an opening in the roof a crescent Moon hangs silver in an indigo sky. Its light pools on a double-cube altar at the centre, draped in violet, with a single flame burning on it. Beside the altar stands the image of this sphere: a beautiful naked man, very strong, still as a statue and yet plainly alive. Take your place before the altar, facing east. Draw a full breath and vibrate the divine name of Yesod so that it rolls outward and fills the whole temple: Shaddai El Chai. Feel the nine walls take up the sound and hold it.

rows.title: Calling Gabriel
rows.text: Call on the archangel of this sphere, aloud or in your mind: 'Gabriel, archangel of Yesod, be present and guard this working.' Behind the altar the violet light gathers and brightens until a tall figure stands there, robed in silver and violet, bringing the cool smell of night air over water. You need not see a face clearly. Feel the presence as calm, watchful and steady. At the corners of your sight you may sense the Kerubim, the angelic choir of this sphere, as a soft stirring of wings. Tell Gabriel that you mean to walk the path of Tzaddi toward Netzach and to return by the same road. Wait until you feel the request has been received. Then look to the wall ahead and to your right, where a curtain glows scarlet.

rows.title: The Veil of Tzaddi
rows.text: Walk to the curtain. It is painted with Atu IV, The Emperor, as Crowley and Harris made it: a crowned king enthroned in blazing red and orange, the pillars of his throne topped with the heads of wild mountain rams, a sceptre in one hand and an orb in the other. Study it until the image is sharp. Then raise your right hand and, with the index finger, trace the letter Tzaddi, צ, on the curtain in brilliant scarlet light, the King-scale colour of Aries. See it hang and burn in front of the painted king. Breathe in and vibrate the letter's name: Tzaddi (tsah-DEE). The letter flares, and the curtain parts down its centre. Step through, and feel it fall closed behind you.

rows.title: The Scarlet Country
rows.text: You stand on a rising road at the first edge of dawn. The light is scarlet. It deepens to red in the hollows and flares to bright flame wherever it touches the tops of the stones. The air is cold and clean, the air of early spring, and a wind from ahead carries the sharp resin of dragon's blood. Behind and below you, the violet dusk of Yesod lies like a quiet lake. The road climbs and curves toward a distant glow of green. Walk slowly. Feel the ground under your feet: hard reddish rock, veined with iron. Everything here seems newly begun, as though the land were made this morning. This is the Natural Intelligence, through which everything beneath the Sun is brought to its full nature. Let yourself feel that quickening.

rows.title: The Ram, the Owl and the Hook
rows.text: A clear, fast stream runs beside the road, flowing down toward the lunar waters behind you. Tiger lilies grow along its banks, orange-red and speckled, among low clumps of scarlet geranium. On a ledge above, a wild ram stands against the brightening sky with heavy, curled horns, watching you without fear. Farther on, an owl sits in a bare tree, still awake at the end of its night. Notice how each creature looks at you, and how you feel under its gaze. Then look down into the stream. Something glints there: a hook of bright metal, curved like the letter you traced. Consider it without hurry. A hook reaches into the water and draws up what lives there. Notice what the road itself seems to be doing as it curves upward from the waters, and let any understanding come in its own time.

rows.title: The Throne of the Emperor
rows.text: The road levels onto a high plateau. There, with the rising Sun at its back, stands a throne whose two pillars are crowned with the carved heads of Himalayan rams. On it sits the Emperor, crowned and robed in red and gold. Look at the shape he makes. His head and arms form a triangle pointing upward, and his crossed legs form a cross beneath it: the alchemical sign of sulphur. In one hand he holds a sceptre topped with a ram's head. In the other he holds an orb with a cross on top. A shield leans against the throne, bearing a double-headed eagle and a red disc. At his feet a lamb lies quietly beside a banner. Behind him the Sun clears the horizon. Take in the whole scene, and feel the steady heat that comes from it.

rows.title: The Emperor's Answer
rows.text: Approach the throne and stop at a respectful distance. Greet the Emperor in your own words, and give a sign of greeting if you use one. Tell him you have come up from Yesod by the path of Tzaddi, and ask him plainly: what does this path have to teach me? Then fall quiet and wait. He may speak, show you something, place an object in your hand, or simply look at you. The answer may arrive as a word, an image, a feeling or a memory. Receive whatever comes without judging or editing it, and do not hurry to interpret it. If nothing seems to happen, rest in the silence; that is worth recording too. When the exchange feels complete, thank him, and ask his leave to look toward the end of the road.

rows.title: The Threshold of Netzach
rows.text: Walk on past the throne. The road climbs one last short rise, and the scarlet light softens and mingles with green. At the crest you reach a threshold and stop. Before you, a little way off, stands a seven-sided temple glowing emerald, its edges touched with amber. The scent of roses drifts toward you. Low in the paling sky above it burns Venus, the morning star, brighter than anything around her. Through the open doorway you may glimpse the image of this sphere, a beautiful naked woman, and hear the name YHVH Tzabaoth sounding faintly from within. Do not enter; this is as far as today's journey goes. Simply look, breathe the rose-scented air, and let the sight of Victory settle into you.

rows.title: The Return
rows.text: Turn and walk back down the road the way you came. Bow to the Emperor as you pass the throne. Pass the owl in its tree, the ram on its ledge, and the lilies and geraniums by the stream with its bright hook. The scarlet deepens toward red, and below you the violet of Yesod widens. Soon the curtain hangs before you, with the painted Emperor now seen from behind, glowing faintly. Step through into the temple of Yesod. Turn and see the letter Tzaddi still burning on the curtain. Trace it once in reverse, or draw your hand down through it, and watch the scarlet fade until the curtain hangs plain and closed. Face the altar and thank Gabriel for guarding your way. Vibrate once more: Shaddai El Chai.

rows.title: Grounding
rows.text: Let the temple of Yesod grow dim: the violet walls, the altar flame, the Moon above. Let it fade like a room at dusk until only you remain. Become aware of your body in the chair again: its weight, the pressure of your feet on the floor, your hands on your thighs. Take a deeper breath and listen to the sounds of the room around you. Wriggle your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and gently turn your head. When you are ready, open your eyes and rest them on something solid and ordinary. Say your name quietly aloud. Before you move on to anything else, take up your journal and write down everything you remember, above all what the Emperor gave you.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright with your bare feet flat on the floor. This path rules the legs and feet, so let them be felt. Rest your hands on your thighs. The crimson candle burns low, the room is dim, and a faint sweetness of ambergris hangs in the air. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold for four. Keep it slow and effortless. On each out-breath release a little more: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, belly, thighs, calves, the soles of the feet. Feel the body's weight drain down into the ground. When the rhythm runs by itself, let go of counting, and let the darkness behind your eyes become a space waiting to be entered.

rows.title: The Temple of Malkuth
rows.text: Build the temple of Malkuth around you. It is a square hall of solid stone, and its floor is divided into four quarters of citrine, olive, russet and black, the Queen-scale colours of the Kingdom. The walls are plain and sturdy, and a double-cube altar stands at the centre. The air smells of earth after rain and, faintly, of dittany. Beside the altar is the magical image of this sphere: a young woman, crowned and throned, calm and entirely present. Facing east, take a deep breath and vibrate the Divine Name: Adonai Melekh. Feel the stone answer through the soles of your feet. Then call the archangel Sandalphon, and sense a tall presence arrive beside you, rooted and patient, whose attention reaches down into the ground and up toward the heights at once.

rows.title: The Veil of Qoph
rows.text: There are three doors in the eastern wall. The one right of centre, toward the south-east, is hung with a curtain painted with Atu XVIII, The Moon: a waning crescent above, two dark towers, jackal-headed figures at the gate, and a beetle in the water below. Raise your hand and trace on the curtain the letter Qoph, ק, in lines of deep crimson light. It has a curved head-stroke, and beneath it a separate stem that drops below the line, like a skull and the spine hanging from it. As it glows, vibrate its name: Qoph. Feel the sound at the base of your skull. The curtain darkens and softens, like water seen from above at night. Sandalphon remains in the temple. Step through, and feel coolness close around you and then part.

rows.title: The Shore of Night
rows.text: You stand at the edge of dark water under a night sky. The light is a crimson so deep it seems almost beyond sight, the King-scale colour of this path. Where it thins, it turns buff flecked with silver, like moonlight on sand. The shore is wet, and your bare feet sink a little at each step. Mangroves stand with their roots in the tide. In the shallows a great beetle works with patient effort, rolling a disc of dim gold before it. This is Khephra, carrying the Sun beneath the water through the hours of night. Farther out a fish turns, and a dolphin's back curves briefly out of the sea and is gone. The air smells of salt, weed and sweet musk. A path of pale stone rises from the waterline and leads inland.

rows.title: Between the Towers
rows.text: Follow the path up from the shore. Ahead it passes between two dark towers, blank and windowless, standing like the posts of a gate. Above them hangs the waning Moon, and drops fall slowly from its lower edge, each shaped like a small Yod. Before each tower stands a tall figure with the head of a jackal, still as carved stone, and at their feet two jackals wait with lowered heads. Fear may come here: a tightening in the belly, a sense of something behind you, shapes at the edge of sight that shift between human and animal. Do not run, and do not argue with them. Keep walking at the same pace, breathing slowly. This is the Corporeal Intelligence, the old wisdom that shapes and grows every body and speaks in the language of instinct.

rows.title: The Moving Water
rows.text: Past the gate the path winds upward through low, silver-dark hills. Pale poppies grow along its edges, and a drowsiness rises from them; notice it and stay awake. A stream runs beside the path, and its water seems to move both ways at once, rising and falling like a slow tide. Kneel and look into it. The surface is a mirror, and the face that looks back may not be quite your own. Watch without judging. On the stream bed lies a pearl, grown layer by layer around a grain of grit. Take it up and hold it in the hollow of your hand. Pisces is the last sign of the zodiac, the sea in which forms dissolve and from which new ones come. Feel your body as a tide that has come and gone many times.

rows.title: The Guide of Souls
rows.text: One of the jackal-headed wardens has left the gate and now walks beside you. This is Anubis, whom the Greeks matched with Hermes, the guide of souls. He is tall and dark, his ears alert, his eyes steady and without malice. He knows this road in darkness as well as by day. Stop, face him, greet him, and ask what this path teaches. Then wait in silence. An answer may come as a word, a picture, a sensation in the body, a scent or an object offered to you. It may be something you do not yet understand. Do not supply the answer yourself or steer it toward what you hoped for. Receive it, and fix it in memory exactly as it comes. Stay here as long as you need.

rows.title: The Threshold of Netzach
rows.text: Thank Anubis. The path climbs a last rise and the night begins to thin. Ahead, where the sky pales, stands a seven-sided temple whose walls glow emerald, the Queen-scale colour of Netzach. Its doorway is wreathed with roses, and the scent of rose and benzoin reaches you on warmer air. Inside you may glimpse the image of this sphere, a beautiful naked woman, or only a shimmer of green and amber like dawn through leaves. This is Victory, the sphere of Venus. Venus is exalted in Pisces, so the dark road has been leading toward beauty all along. Do not enter. Stand at the edge of the light, let it touch your face, and remember what you see.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Turn and go back down the path. The emerald light fades behind you, and the poppies and the tidal stream slip past. The pearl stays with you, along with anything else you were given. Walk between the two towers again; the jackal-headed warden returns to his post and lets you pass. Go down to the shore, where Khephra still rolls the hidden Sun through the dark water. Ahead is the curtain, glowing faintly crimson. Step through into the stone temple of Malkuth and feel the four-coloured floor firm beneath you. Turn to the curtain and trace the letter Qoph once more, drawing it back into the painted veil until its crimson light fades and the trump is still. Then thank the archangel Sandalphon for guarding the Kingdom while you travelled.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Let the temple walls grow thin and fade until only the sense of solid ground remains, and then only the floor of your own room beneath your bare feet. Press your soles down firmly. Feel your calves, your knees, your thighs, and the weight of your body on the chair. Take three fuller breaths. Move your fingers and toes, stretch your legs, and roll your head gently to loosen the back of the neck, where Qoph sits. Listen to the ordinary sounds around you. When you are ready, open your eyes and look slowly around the room, naming a few plain objects. If you feel heavy or dreamy, stand up and stamp your feet. Come fully back before you start thinking about what you saw.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs. Let the orange candle and the frankincense stay at the edge of your attention. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep it easy, never strained. With each out-breath let one part of the body soften in turn: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the backs of the legs. Feel your weight settle downward while the spine stays light and tall. When the rhythm carries itself, let the counting fall away. The room grows quieter, and your attention turns inward, toward the space behind your closed eyes, which is ready to take shape.

rows.title: The Temple of Yesod
rows.text: Build the temple of Yesod around you. It is a nine-sided chamber whose walls glow a soft violet, the Queen-scale colour of the Foundation, and whose floor is cool and faintly silvered, like wet sand under moonlight. A crescent moon hangs in the violet dome above. The air smells of jasmine and of damp roots. At the centre stands an altar, and beside it, still as a statue yet breathing, is the magical image of this sphere: a beautiful naked man, very strong, standing on the foundation that holds up everything built above it. Face east. Draw a full breath and vibrate the Divine Name: Shaddai El Chai. Let it roll out through the nine walls. Then call the archangel Gabriel, and feel a presence gather at your side, cool as rain, attentive and calm.

rows.title: The Veil of Resh
rows.text: In the wall to your left as you face east, toward the north-east, hangs a curtain you had not noticed before. Painted on it is Atu XIX, The Sun: a great disc of light with twelve rays, a green hill beneath, and two winged children dancing there. Raise your hand and trace on the curtain the letter Resh, ר, in lines of clear orange light: a single stroke that runs level and then turns down, like a brow and the profile of a head. As it glows, vibrate its name: Resh. Feel the sound warm your chest. The curtain turns translucent, lit from behind as if by morning. Gabriel remains in the temple; this road you walk yourself. Step through the painted light and feel it pass over your face like the first sun on a cold day.

rows.title: The Road of the Sun
rows.text: You stand on a road of pale, packed earth that climbs gently ahead. The light here is orange, the King-scale colour of the path. Toward the horizon it deepens into rich amber, and overhead it brightens to gold. There are almost no shadows; the air itself seems lit. On both sides, fields of sunflowers hold their heavy faces toward a brightness further on that you cannot yet look at directly. Laurel grows along the verges, dark and glossy, giving off a sharp green smell when you brush it, and small purple heliotrope turns with the light. Beneath these scents you catch a faint trace of frankincense and cinnamon. Walk slowly. Feel warmth settle on your forehead and face, for Resh is the head, and let the light find whatever in you has been kept in shade.

rows.title: The Hill and the Children
rows.text: The road rises to a round green hill, and you see that a low wall runs around its base. The wall is well built and solid, but it encloses nothing overhead: above the hill the sky is completely open. On the summit two children are dancing, each with bright, patterned wings like a butterfly's. They are not performing for you; they are simply at play, and their play makes the whole hill feel lighter. Above them the Sun hangs vast and near, its twelve rays reaching out toward the ring of the zodiac, the twelve signs set around the sky like a slow wheel. This is the Lord of the Fire of the World. Stand by the wall and watch. Notice what in you wants to join the dance, and what holds back.

rows.title: The Lion, the Hawk and the Stone
rows.text: A lion walks out of the tall grass and lies down across the road ahead of you, unhurried, its mane catching the light like a second small sun. It does not threaten; it simply fills the way with its whole weight, and you walk around it with respect. A sparrowhawk circles overhead, then settles on a laurel branch and watches the ground with complete attention. In the dust at your feet lies a clear yellow-green stone, a chrysolite; pick it up and feel it warm in your palm. This is the Collecting Intelligence, where scattered things are gathered: the images of Yesod, the words of Hod, the patterns of the stars. Feel your own scattered thoughts drawing together, like sunlight brought to a single point through a lens.

rows.title: The Guide
rows.text: Where the road levels near the top of the rise, a figure waits in the full light. It has a man's body and a hawk's head, and above its brow rests the disc of the Sun, circled by a serpent. This is Ra, as the path's attributions give him. If a golden archer with a bow appears instead, that is Apollo, who also belongs to this road. Greet the figure in whatever way feels right, and ask plainly what this path teaches. Then be quiet. You may receive a word, an image, a gesture or something placed in your hand, or only a warmth you cannot name. Do not reach for an answer you expected. Let whatever comes, come, and hold it in memory exactly as it is. Take all the time you need.

rows.title: The Threshold of Hod
rows.text: Thank your guide. Beyond the hill the road runs on toward a building on the rise ahead: an eight-sided hall whose walls shine orange, the Queen-scale colour of Hod. Fine letters and numbers are cut into its surfaces, and they seem to rearrange themselves as you look. A trace of storax drifts down to you. Through the open doorway you may glimpse the poised figure of the Hermaphrodite, or only light moving over polished stone. This is Splendour, the sphere of Mercury, of language, number and measure. Do not go in. For today it is enough to see it from the end of the Sun's road and to know that the path you have walked arrives here. Let the image of the hall settle into memory.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Turn back the way you came. Walk down past the walled hill and the dancing children and past the lion resting in the grass, while the sparrowhawk watches you go. Carry whatever you were given. The orange light softens with each step, sliding toward amber and then toward a quiet violet as the road descends. Ahead is the curtain, seen now from its far side and glowing. Step through into the nine-sided temple of Yesod. Turn to face the veil and trace the letter Resh again, as though drawing it back into the curtain. Watch its orange light fade until only the painted trump remains, still and closed. Then turn to Gabriel, waiting beside the altar, and thank the archangel for keeping the Foundation while you travelled.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Let the temple of Yesod grow thin, its violet walls turning transparent, until only the sense of the altar remains, and then only your own body sitting in the room. Feel your feet on the floor and the chair beneath you. Take three breaths a little deeper than before. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and notice the sounds around you, the temperature of the air and the scent of the incense. When you are ready, open your eyes and look at a few ordinary objects, naming them to yourself. Stamp your feet lightly or press your palms firmly together. Do not rush to interpret anything yet. First come fully back.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright with your feet flat on the floor, hands on your thighs and spine tall. Close your eyes and take up the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, empty for four. Keep the count gentle. As you breathe, notice the warmth in your body: the heat of blood moving through you, the pulse at your wrists and throat, the steady circulation that 777 assigns to this path. With each out-breath let tension go from the brow, jaw, neck, shoulders, chest, belly, hips, legs and feet. Let your weight sink into the chair and the floor, and allow the room to recede. When your breath is slow and even and your attention rests quietly inside you, begin.

rows.title: The Temple of Malkuth
rows.text: You are standing in the temple of Malkuth. Underfoot is the chequered floor of black and white. Around you the walls hold the four Queen-scale colours of this sphere, citrine, olive, russet and black, like the quarters of a single circle. Today notice the russet especially, the colour of fire within earth. A black altar stands at the centre with a flame burning on it. Near it sits the young woman, crowned and throned, who is the image of the Kingdom. In the eastern wall hang three veils. Stand at the altar facing East and vibrate: Adonai Melekh. Feel the name resonate down through the floor. Then call: Sandalphon. The archangel's presence gathers, tall and quiet, as though the whole temple had drawn breath. Ask for guidance and protection on the path of Fire, and wait for the sense that it is granted.

rows.title: The Veil of Shin
rows.text: Go to the veil on the side of the Pillar of Severity, the one that leads toward Hod. On it is painted Atu XX, The Aeon. The star-bodied goddess Nuit arches across the top, with a winged globe of fire beneath her. Below them the hawk-headed god sits enthroned, and before him stands a translucent child with a finger at his lips. At the foot is the letter Shin, with human figures rising in its three flames. Raise your hand and trace the letter Shin, ש, in glowing orange-scarlet, feeling heat at your fingertips. Vibrate the name of the letter: Shin. The painted colours brighten until the curtain seems to burn without being consumed. Give the Sign of the Enterer and step through.

rows.title: The Land of Perpetual Fire
rows.text: You come out into heat and light. The sky here is a glowing orange-scarlet, like the heart of a forge, and the ground under your feet is warm red rock veined with vermilion. Where the light catches it, flecks of gold spark in the scarlet, and here and there you see a shimmer of crimson and emerald, as at the core of a flame. Low fires burn along the way with no fuel and no smoke, each one steady and unending. The air smells of frankincense. Between the fires grow red poppies and hibiscus, dark stands of nettle, and scarlet flowers of every kind. Feel the heat on your face and hands; it warms you but does not burn. Walk forward, and notice how your body answers the fire in your heartbeat, your blood and your breath.

rows.title: Sun, Moon, Salamander and Lion
rows.text: As you walk, look up. The sun and the moon cross the burning sky, each keeping its own course, neither overtaking the other. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this path the Perpetual Intelligence because it keeps the sun and moon in their ordered motions. Feel that order beneath all the heat around you. Now look down into the fires beside the road. Salamanders move within them, the elemental beings of Fire, quick, bright and curious. Watch them without reaching for them. Ahead of you a lion lies across the path. It is the Kerub of Fire, tawny and gold, its mane stirring in the rising heat. Stop before it, stand upright and still, and let it take your measure. When it rises and walks beside you, or moves aside, go on.

rows.title: The Old Judgement and the New Aeon
rows.text: The path opens onto a broad plain, and here you see the old image of this trump: rows of stone tombs under a dim sky, and a great angel raising a trumpet to wake the dead. It is the Judgement of the old tarot. As you watch, the angel's note sounds and the scene changes. The dim sky becomes the dark-blue body of Nuit, arched from horizon to horizon and strewn with stars. Beneath her a globe of fire opens its wings. The tombs are gone. In their place the letter Shin rises as a great triple flame, and from each of its three tongues a human figure lifts upward, as if being born rather than raised. Stand in the heat of it. Consider what in you is ready to wake, and what is ready to burn away.

rows.title: The Guide
rows.text: A figure comes toward you from the centre of the flame. It may be a hawk-headed god, crowned, clothed in scarlet and gold and bearing a wand: Horus, lord of this Aeon, as he sits enthroned on the Stele. He may instead come as the silent child with a finger to his lips, or something else entirely may come. Whoever approaches, test it: trace the letter Shin before it in orange-scarlet flame and vibrate the letter name. A true guide stands firm or grows brighter, and anything false wavers and fades. When you are satisfied, greet the figure with respect and ask what this path has to teach you. Then keep silent. Let the answer come in its own form and its own time: a word, an image, a sensation, a symbol placed in your hands, or nothing yet. Remain for as long as the meeting lasts.

rows.title: The Threshold of Hod
rows.text: When the meeting ends, the path climbs a little further and comes to a threshold. The fire thins here, and the scarlet light shades into a clear, bright orange, the Queen-scale colour of Hod. Through the opening you glimpse a hall of polished surfaces where light is reflected and multiplied, and where figures and letters seem to be written on the air itself. At its centre stands the magical image of Splendour: a hermaphrodite, poised and luminous. You may sense the name Elohim Tzabaoth sounding there, and the presence of the archangel Mikael. Do not cross. Take in the colour and the clarity, and notice how the fire behind you has prepared you for this light. Then bow and turn back.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Retrace the path. Cross the plain where the triple flame of Shin still burns. Pass the lion and the salamanders, the perpetual fires and the scarlet flowers, with the sun and moon still moving in their order overhead. Hold close whatever you received. Your guide may walk part of the way with you; thank it when you part. The veil appears before you, glowing from within. Step through into the temple of Malkuth. Turn and trace the letter Shin on the curtain once more. Then draw your hand downward and watch the scarlet fade from the painted trump; the way is closed. Give the Sign of Silence. Go to the altar, thank Sandalphon for guarding your journey, and feel the archangel's presence withdraw.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Let the temple fade around you, its colours sinking into ordinary darkness. Feel the chair beneath you and the floor under your feet. Notice the temperature of the room, which is probably cooler than the path you have just walked, and let your body settle into it. Take three deep breaths. Move your hands and feet, and stretch your neck and shoulders. Say your name aloud. Open your eyes, look slowly around, and name a few ordinary objects. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor. If you feel lightheaded or overheated, drink some water and rest both palms flat on the floor for a moment. Then record what you experienced before speaking to anyone or doing anything else.

rows.title: Settle
rows.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat, hands resting on your thighs, spine straight but not stiff. If you know the God-form of the seated Egyptian, take it. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the rhythm become even and unforced. With each exhalation release one region of the body: the jaw and brow, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs, the soles of the feet. Notice the weight of your body resting on the chair, the chair resting on the floor, and the floor resting on the earth itself. This path begins in the body and in matter, so first let yourself be fully here. When the breath runs on its own, let the room grow dim and quiet around you.

rows.title: The Temple of Malkuth
rows.text: Around you a temple takes shape. The floor is a pavement of black and white squares, cool beneath your feet. The walls glow in the Queen-scale colours of Malkuth: citrine, olive, russet and black. Citrine is highest, toward the East before you, and black is deepest, down toward the ground. At the centre stands a double-cube altar draped in black, with a lamp burning above it and a small dish of salt beside it. In the eastern wall hang three veils. Near the altar sits the magical image of this sphere: a young woman, crowned and throned, calm and watchful. Stand at the altar, facing East, and vibrate the Divine Name: Adonai Melekh. Feel the syllables settle into the floor. Then call the archangel: Sandalphon. A tall presence gathers beyond the altar, robed in the colours of earth, and inclines its head. Ask Sandalphon's protection for your journey, and wait until you sense it given.

rows.title: The Veil of Tau
rows.text: Walk to the East. Of the three veils, go to the central one, which leads straight up the Middle Pillar. It is a heavy curtain, and on it is painted Atu XXI, The Universe: a naked dancer within a great ellipse of small rings, a serpent coiling about her, the four Kerubic heads at the corners, and at the foot the outline of a building of many chambers. Raise your hand and trace the letter Tau, ת, on the curtain in deep indigo light, its strokes glowing where your fingers pass. Vibrate the name of the letter: Tau. The painted figures deepen and seem to stir, and the curtain thins like smoke. Give the Sign of the Enterer, projecting yourself forward, and step through with Sandalphon's presence at your back.

rows.title: The Onyx Road
