rows.text: You stand on a road that runs gently upward through the night. The sky is deep indigo, darkening toward the horizon to blue-black. The road beneath you is paved with onyx, bands of black and white laid in a slow, even rhythm. The air is cool and still. Dark trees grow on either side: yew and cypress and ancient ash, and in their shade the low leaves of nightshade and the pale cups of hellebore. Nothing here hurries, and your own steps slow to match the place. Overhead, seven lights move across the indigo. They are the seven planets, weaving and never colliding. This is the Administrative Intelligence of the Sepher Yetzirah, the path that directs the seven wandering stars and keeps each to its own course. Walk on, and watch them turn.

rows.title: The River and the Crocodile
rows.text: The road descends to a broad, slow river. Its water is black, faintly rayed with blue, as if the night sky had been poured out and gathered here. A low bridge of stone crosses it, though its far end fades into mist. At the water's edge a great crocodile lies motionless, its eyes just above the surface. It is the beast of Sebek and Mako, the gods 777 sets on this path. Do not hurry past it, and do not fear it. Stop and greet it with respect. It regards you for a long time, with the patience of something that has watched this river for ages. Notice what you feel under that gaze, whether it is heaviness, stillness, age or something else. When the crocodile sinks back or lets its eyes close, cross the bridge.

rows.title: The Dancer in the Ellipse
rows.text: Beyond the river the land opens into a wide plain beneath the turning planets, and ahead of you the trump comes alive. A vast ellipse of small rings stands upright in the air, seventy-two of them linked like a wreath. Within it a woman dances, naked, balanced and unhurried. A great serpent coils about her as she moves, and she turns its coils as easily as a dancer turns a ribbon, so that its spiral and her movement become one motion. At the four quarters around the ellipse you sense the Kerubim: bull, lion, eagle and human face. Far below her feet rises a vast building of many small rooms, each room one of the elements of matter. Stand here and feel that the dance, the serpent and the solid house are one thing: the finished world, sealed and still alive.

rows.title: The Guide
rows.text: The dance slows, and the dancer steps down out of the ellipse to stand before you. Something else may come instead, such as an aged, grey-bearded figure with a sickle, the god of time and limits whose planet rules this path. If so, let it come. Look carefully at whatever figure approaches, and test it: trace the Tau before it in indigo and vibrate the letter name again. A true guide of this path holds steady or grows clearer, and anything false fades or breaks apart. When you are satisfied, greet it and ask plainly what this path has to teach you. Then be silent. Let the answer come in its own form: a word, an image, a gesture, a feeling, or nothing at all. If you are offered a symbol, accept it and hold it. Stay with this meeting for as long as it lasts.

rows.title: The Threshold of Yesod
rows.text: When the meeting is complete, the road carries you a little further, to where it ends at a threshold. Before you rises a doorway filled with violet light, the Queen-scale colour of Yesod, silvered at its edges like moonlight on water. Through it you glimpse a hall of violet and silver, and at its centre the magical image of the Foundation: a beautiful naked man, very strong, standing as though he bears the weight of everything around him. Behind him you sense vast, slow movement, tides and pulses, the turning wheels of the world's hidden machinery. Far off the name Shaddai El Chai is sounding, and you may feel the presence of Gabriel. Do not cross. This is the edge of today's journey. Take in what you can, bow, and turn back.

rows.title: Return
rows.text: Walk back the way you came. Your guide may go with you to the edge of the plain or leave you there; thank it either way. Pass the ellipse, now still, and cross the bridge over the black-blue river. Follow the onyx road down between the yews and cypresses, with the seven planets turning above you. Hold close whatever you were given. At the end of the road the veil hangs before you, and you see the painted trump from its reverse side. Step through into the temple of Malkuth. Turn to face the veil and trace the letter Tau on it once more. Then draw your hand downward and watch the indigo fade from the curtain; the passage is closed. Give the Sign of Silence. Return to the altar, thank Sandalphon for guarding your way, and feel the presence withdraw.

rows.title: Ground
rows.text: Let the temple of Malkuth grow faint around you, its colours sinking into the ordinary darkness behind your eyelids. Feel the chair again, the weight of your body, the floor under your feet, and the air on your hands and face. Take three breaths fuller than before. Move your fingers and toes, and roll your shoulders. Say your own name quietly aloud. When you are ready, open your eyes, look around the room, and name a few ordinary things you see. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor two or three times, and know that you are fully back. Before doing anything else, write down what you saw and what you received.
